articleTitle: Investigation of impedance compensation for inductive via holes using capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Via holes are widely used in printed circuit boards (PCBs) to connect the traces distributed in different layers. Sometimes, via holes are inductive and lead to impedance discontinuity in connection area, which may reduce signal integrity of circuit board. In the current work, a novel impedance compensation strategy for the inductive via holes was presented. Compared with the traditional compensation strategy using grounding via holes, compensation strategy using capacitors has a better electrical performance in low frequency band.

articleTitle: A Novel Translucent Lowpass Filter Design Using Asymmetric Pi-shaped DGS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a translucent low-pass filter for microstrip lines is designed based on an asymmetric Pi-shaped structure. It is fabricated by using flexible material PET and metallic copper with dimensions of 150 mm × 7.8 mm × 0.148 mm. The proposed low-pass filter has a narrow transition band. The insertion loss of the filter less than 1.5 dB below 0.32 GHz and a wide stop band from 1.59 GHz to 6.50 GHz with insertion loss greater than 30 dB. The transparency of the proposed translucent low-pass filter is increased by adding square holes on the copper layer. We cascade multiple identical structures to increase the insertion loss of the stopband without affecting the passband. The proposed translucent low-pass filter is flexibility, high transparency, and high insertion loss in the stopband. These features make it an ideal candidate for use in applications that require electromagnetic protection while maintaining a clear field of view, such as vehicle communication and building house communication. Overall, it provides a new approach to transparent filter design and has the potential to greatly benefit various industries.

articleTitle: A Low-Pass Filtering Cable Design for Sub-6 GHz Wireless Communication Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel design concept for a filtering cable optimized for sub-6 GHz wireless communication applications. We introduce a groundbreaking approach that incorporates an insulated cylinder coated with a defected conductor transmission structure (DCTS). The integration of the DCTS enables distributed lowpass filtering advantages along the cable's axis, specifically tailored for the sub-6GHz frequency range. The DCTS, comprising six-slot-ring defected structures, functions as an equivalent lumped filtering circuit, allowing easy fine-tuning of the filtering performance by manipulating the geometrical parameters of the six-slot-ring defected structure. Our meticulous engineering efforts result in a meticulously engineered low-pass filtering cable, constructed with a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) inner core wire, enveloped by a flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) featuring 40 etched six-slot-ring defected structures. A layer of PTFE serves as the transmission dielectric, while an outermost shielding layer enhances the shielding effectiveness (SE). The proposed filtering cable, with a radius of 2.413mm and a length of 340mm, exhibits exceptional performance characteristics tailored to sub-6GHz wireless communication applications. It achieves an insertion loss of below 0.38 dB within the passband range below 6 GHz and provides rejection levels exceeding 43 dB within the stopband range from 7.7 GHz to 25 GHz. Compared to conventional filters, the proposed filtering cable offers a more versatile and compact solution, delivering outstanding filtering capabilities specifically designed for sub-6 GHz wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: A Fast Shooting and Bouncing Ray Algorithm for Electromagnetics Scattering Based on Bounding Volume Hierarchy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Utilized a surface area heuristic (SAH) and bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) algorithm to accelerate ray tracing in the shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) algorithm, enabling fast computation of the scattering field for objects. The method use the SAH to partition all triangular elements and allocates them to different bounding boxes. By performing intersection calculations on bounding boxes at different levels, non-intersecting triangles are swiftly discarded, significantly reduce intersection computations. The computational results demonstrate that the method achieves lower computation times at all orders compared to the reference algorithm.

articleTitle: An Experimental Analysis of the Effects of Ground Wires During Conducted Emission Current Probe Method Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of ground wires and wiring harness arrangements during conducted emission current probe method measurements are experimentally analyzed. The analysis shows that RF signal transmission path in the measurements is significantly affected by the different wiring harness conditions such as ground wire routing position, wiring harness tightly / loosely bundled. Especially, in the low-frequency range below 20 MHz, whether the ground wires are included in the current probe has a significant impact on the measurement results.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Spurious Suppression Techniques of S-band Magnetrons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Magnetrons are good candidates for large power microwave sources in various industrial applications. They are unstable oscillators with frequency and amplitude fluctuations, which easily cause electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems. Two regular methods to improve magnetrons' spectrum purity are compared in experiments using 1-kW S-band cook-type magnetrons. One method is to depress anode voltage ripple, which reduces the output frequency fluctuation range to 7.9%• The other method is injection-locking, which reduces the range to 1%. The injection-locking technique is more suitable for applications with requirements of high-frequency stability and controllability. Only low spurious noise and high-frequency purity are required in a few industrial applications. It is an economically feasible approach to depressing the voltage ripple by reducing filament current and adding a capacitor-based filter module. The study provides a reference to suppressing the EMI caused by magnetrons in different demands and scenarios.

articleTitle: Flexible MXene/Ag nanowires composite film for high-performance electromagnetic shielding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Flexible electromagnetic shielding films have attracted wide attention due to their excellent electromagnetic shielding performance and flexible compact nature. In this paper, a composite film was prepared by combining two-dimensional (2D) transition metal carbonitrides (MXene) with silver nanowires (AgNWs). The AgNWs-induced surface wrinkles of MXene played a dominate role in enhancing its electromagnetic wave absorption properties. Significantly, as-fabricated composite film exhibited electromagnetic shielding performance of up to 60 dB in the X-band (8–12 GHz), where a 70 % increase in absorption of electromagnetic waves was realized compared with the pure MXene films. Additionally, the composite film demonstrated strong mechanical stability with the electromagnetic shielding efficiency remained at 99.65 % even after several hundred bending cycles.

articleTitle: A Wideband Spread Spectrum Reception Structure Based on Coherent Dual Optical Carriers and Superheterodyne Photonic Down Conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes and demonstrates a novel microwave photonic receiving structure that employs two-stage superheterodyne with ultra-wideband tunable coherent dual optical carriers. This technique enables the down-conversion and despread of high frequency broadband spread spectrum signals, while ensuring ideal suppression of image frequency. The results demonstrate high performance in microwave photonic receiving of the proposed method.

articleTitle: On the Harmonic Wave Emitting Characteristics of the Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The phase characteristics of harmonic wave of array antennas are analyzed. The harmonic wave emitting characteristics of the array antennas are achieved by the simulation the linear and planar array antennas. The array antennas emitting of harmonic wave are directional. When the beam direction of work frequency scan in the sky the harmonic emitting direction change as well.

articleTitle: Clutter Suppression Approach Based on AI for Wideband Microwave Photonic Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper focuses on exploring the effectiveness of AI in clutter suppression based on microwave photonic radar. Clutter is generally defined as scattered echoes from objects other than the target, and these clutter powers can sometimes be much stronger than even the target's echo signal, which makes the detection of target echoes by radar very difficult. The hourglass network, as a new convolutional network structure, can process the features of the target at all scales of the image and capture the spatial information associated with the target. Therefore, an attempt is made to process the imaging results of radar ISAR with hourglass network to learn the feature information of target imaging and thus suppress the display of clutter.

articleTitle: Discontinuous Galerkin Based JMCFIE for Computing Electromagnetic Scattering by Objects with Large and Deep Cavities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A discontinuous Galerkin (DG) based Electric and Magnetic Current Combined-Field Integral Equation (JMCFIE) method is proposed in this paper for accurately computing electromagnetic scattering by objects with large and deep cavities. The implementation of DG allows conformal and nonconformal surface discretization, which brings significant flexibility in the meshing of large and multiscale objects. The lower triangular approximate Schur preconditioner (LTASP) is combined with Multi-Level Fast Multipole Algorithm (MLFMA) to accelerate the convergence of GMRES iteration. Numerical experiments are shown in this paper to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on In-House Verification Method of 150Ω Direct Coupling Probe for IC EMC Test
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: An in-house verification method of the 150Ω direct coupling probe which is an important device of 150Ω direct coupling method for IC EMC test has been proposed. This method which can effectively meet the requirements of the in-house verification is simple to operate and has good consistency. The applicable frequency range of this method is 1MHz to 20MHz.

articleTitle: A Tunable Bandstop Filtering Cable for Wide-Bandwidth Interference Suppression
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a tunable band-stop filtering cable for wide-bandwidth interference suppression while the signal is in transit in it. A seminal cable modal that wrapping an insulated core wire in a defected conductor transmission structure (DCTS) is introduced. The band-stop filtering cable proposed consists of a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) core wrapped in a defected conductor layer, a transmission dielectric PTFE layer, and the outermost shielding layer to strengthen shielding performance. The single-frequency band-stop filtering cable loaded with one rectangular spiral resonator can be equivalent to a parallel LC resonant circuit, and the resonant frequency can be modulated by tuning up the parameters of defected structure. We provide an elaborate analysis about the impact of variation in each parameter of defected structure on resonance frequency. The simulation results indicate that the resonant frequency is 3 GHz, the insertion loss is 25 dB and the return loss is 0.1dB. In addition, a wide-bandwidth filtering cable cascaded with twenty-one resonator units was fabricated and tested. Its radius is 2.413 mm and its length is 175 mm. The EM simulation results indicated a wide stopband from 3GHz to 5 GHz, and suppression of up to 60dB and a very narrow transition band. Compared with traditional communication cables, filtering cable can greatly improve the integration of microwave circuits by distributed suppressing unwanted harmonic components while providing transmission and shielding performance.

articleTitle: Photonic THz Frequency Domain Spectroscopy System with Attenuated Total Reflection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a THz frequency domain attenuated total reflection (ATR) spectroscopy system using photomixing coherent detection. In our work, the terahertz signal is generated through the optical beat of two DFB lasers, and mixed with the same beat note using a time delay. Since one of the DFB lasers works in frequency sweep mode, we obtain the THz spectra in the range of 0.2-1.2THz with a dynamic range of over 60dB and a frequent resolution of 100MHz. In addition, we propose to insert an ATR prism in the spatial optical path to enable direct detection of polar liquids and solids, which have strong absorption of the terahertz waves. We demonstrate the measurement of the dielectric constant of distilled water with the proposed technique, the results are consistent with the calculated results from the Liebe model.

articleTitle: A 2~3.6 GHz Reconfigurable Bandpass Filter Based on GaAs Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an on-chip reconfigurable filter based on GaAs process is designed. The filter is constructed by cascading low- and high-pass filters and employs the Butterworth prototype as the basic structure of the two filters. The combination of varactor and switching capacitor arrays composed of pHEMT transistors is used to realize a wide capacitance tuning range. Meanwhile, transmission zeros in the form of series resonances are introduced at the lower and upper stopband of the bandpass filter to improve selectivity and out-of-band rejection. One on-chip reconfigurable bandpass filter with continuously reconfigurable center frequency is designed and fabricated using the 0.15um GaAs pHEMT process. In this design, the wide tunable center frequency range covers 2~3.6GHz, the 1dB bandwidth is fixed at 800MHz, and the stopband rejection is greater than 28dB.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characteriation of STT-MRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This study delves into the electromagnetic attributes of STT-MRAM, emphasizing the implications of its intrinsic chip architecture on both its emission and immunity properties. We embarked on an exhaustive exploration and validation of STT-MRAM's radiated electromagnetic emissions, conducted emissions, and conducted immunity. The findings underscore that diverse operational modes and package features wield substantial influence on the electromagnetic behavior of STT-MRAM.

articleTitle: Design of a Circularly-Polarized Miniaturized Microstrip Annular Ring Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A design approach to obtain a miniaturization, semi-circular, slotted annular ring antenna with circularly-polarized (CP) radiation is presented in this paper. Firstly, the antenna is miniaturized on the basis of a traditional annular ring antenna, which can reduce the overall transverse size by nearly 50%. After that, good CP radiation characteristics is well achieved under a single-point feed by simply loading a horizontal sector slot on the annular ring. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna has a −10dB impedance bandwidth of 11.3% and an axial ratio bandwidth of 3.8%.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Tunable Phase Shifter Based on Signal-Interaction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This article introduces a compact tunable phase shifter consisting of two T-shaped structures based on transversal signal-interaction concepts to achieve wide operating bandwidth. The analysis indicates that a large phase shift range, a low maximum in-band phase shift range fluctuation, and a small size can be achieved through selecting a reasonable transmission line characteristic impedance and electrical length. According to the measured results of experiments, the maximum phase shift range and fluctuation in the operating bandwidth of 1 GHz is 241<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>and 8.2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>respectively. Moreover, the insertion loss at the center frequency of 3.3 GHz varies from 1.2 to 2.98 dB, and the circuit size is 0.18λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> ×0.22λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>.

articleTitle: Deep Gated Recurrent Unit Network for High-Speed Links Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this article, we propose a time domain response modeling method that uses deep gated recurrent gates (GRU) for high-speed links. A high-speed link example is constructed in this paper to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed model. Results show that the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score between predicted and simulated time domain response is up to 0.999, and the eye height and eye width errors are less than 2%. Meanwhile, the proposed model can predict data 50 times faster than Simulink.

articleTitle: A prediction method of electromagnetic pulse effect of HF whip antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Aiming at the demand for predicting the effect of HF whip antenna in high-altitude electromagnetic pulse environment, by modeling the typical HF whip antenna and RF front-end circuit, and using field-path joint simulation to analyze the coupling voltage of antenna port and device port, the simulation results show that the coupling effect of whip antenna on high-altitude electromagnetic pulse is seriously, and the RF front-end device is vulnerable to electromagnetic pulse damage.

articleTitle: A Horn-Tip Ultrawideband E-Probe for Radiated EMI Measurements Up To 50 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Based on a new Horn-Tip structure, this paper introduces a new design for an ultrawideband electric field probe working from 10 kHz up to 50 GHz for better Electromagnetic Compatibility EMC and diagnosis of Electromagnetic Interference EMI. The tip design is based on a Horn shape to enhance and improve the probe efficiency and sensitivity. The probe has been designed on a 4-layer PCB. The probe is divided into 3-parts, the induction part which has the horn-tip structure, the transmission part which is designed by a stripline structure using high-performance dielectrics “Rogers RO4003 (tm)” and “RO4450” with relative permittivity ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>3.55 and 3.3 respectively, and the output part. The probe length is 60 mm with a minimum tip width of 4 mm which is suitable for the narrow and complex PCBs. The stripline transmission part is designed with a slope structure to achieve a good field distribution and enhance impedance matching, resulting in ultra-wide bandwidth scanning. The transfer gain sensitivity is −20 dB at 9 GHz which is about 6 dB higher than some referenced and introduced probes. The spatial resolution is a very narrow result of 0.58 mm when the probe is 0.3 mm above the DUT.

articleTitle: Impact of Electrical Contacts Degradation on High-Speed Digital Signal Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Coaxial connectors are important constituents of high-speed digital systems and play a significant role in transmitting data. The degraded electrical contacts of coaxial connector may result in poor signal integrity and connector failure. In this work, the effects of electrical contacts degradation on digital signal transmission were investigated using model analysis and experimental testing. According to the transmission line theory and the electrical contact theory, an equivalent circuit model of coaxial connector with degraded contact surface was developed. The high frequency parameters were simulated which show good agreement with the measured results. Based on the equivalent models, the performance of different types of digital signals like PRBS and PAM4 signals, was predicted. The eye diagram parameters were simulated and compared for different degradation levels. In addition, digital signal experiments were also conducted for PRBS and PAM4 signals. The results show that the degraded contacts significantly affect the digital signal transmission and lead to contact failure.

articleTitle: A Cone and Ground Plane Device for Calibrating Electromagnetic Pulse Field Sensors and Probes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In order to calibrate the performance of the transient electromagnetic pulse field sensors and probes, this paper developed a cone and ground plane device with a generatrix length of 1 m and a half cone angle of 47°. Based on theoretical analysis, we performed numerical simulation of a cone and ground plane and established a physical device. We utilized a Gaussian pulse with a pulse width of 1.7 ns to excite the cone and ground plane device, tes ted it using a typical D-dot probe to validate the waveform fidelity of the cone and ground plane and provide the probe's amplitude conversion coefficient. Additionally, we also provided the recommended testing area for the cone and ground plane setup.

articleTitle: Photonic-Assisted Enhanced Ranging System Based on QPSK Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a ranging signal demodulation system scheme based on microwave photon technology, which is different from traditional BPSK pseudo-random signal modulation method. This system fully utilizes the orthogonality of channel I and channel Q in Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) signal, and achieves dual pseudo-random code ranging through orthogonal demodulation of the echoes. This improves the signal-to-noise ratio by 3dB after autocorrelation operation, which helps to improve the radar target detection probability and ranging accuracy.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Compatibility Design for Optical Channel of Optoelectronic System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This article presents an electromagnetic compatibility design of optical channel in optoelectronic system based on high impedance surface. Using the characteristics of high impedance surface wave suppression, it is attached to the side wall of the optical channel to achieve the electromagnetic compatibility function with high optical signal transmittance. By changing the arrangement of the protection unit array, the appropriate anti-electromagnetic interference ability and frequency band are designed. In the simulation results, the resisting electromagnetic interference reaches 10 dB in the 1.64 −1.74 GHz and 1.84-2.51 GHz bands. The 10 dB bandwidth reaches 0.77 GHz.

articleTitle: Fast Prediction and Analysis of Target Radar Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a high frequency electromagnetic scattering acceleration method for targets is proposed, which combines CPU multi-core parallel technology, GPU hardware acceleration technology and KD-Tree traversal technology. The high frequency electromagnetic scattering model of complex targets including ships with cavity, angular reflector arrays and ships is established, which can meet the needs of rapid evaluation of large targets. In this paper, a fast prediction method for multiple scattering range image position is proposed. By combining multiple scattering ray diversity with ray path phase prediction theory, the multiple scattering equivalent apparent position of the center is deduced rapidly, and the multipath scattering mechanism and action process of the target containing cavity are revealed. Through the simulation and analysis of ship target, the mapping relationship between the strong scattering contribution formed by multiple scattering of large target and its specific geometric structure is established.

articleTitle: Study on Multipoint Grounding of Harness Shield in Open Area of Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The modeling method of the harness in the open area of the aircraft and the calculation method of the induced current when the electric field irradiates in multiple directions are given. On this basis, the calculation method of the shielding effectiveness improvement caused by multi-point grounding is provided, and the frequency that reaches the maximum value for the first time is also calculated. Meanwhile, the geometric factors that affect the induced current are discussed. In response to the above analytical method, this article finally makes the 3D simulation using FEKO software, and the simulation results are consistent with theoretical calculations. In practical engineering, grounding points should be selected and arranged according to the needs.

Author Keywords: the first frequency of maximum value

articleTitle: Simulation Design of RF Front-End Electromagnetic Pulse Protection Module Based on Gas Discharge Tubes and Transient Voltage Suppressors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: High frequency electromagnetic pulse (EMP) is a major threat to RF front-end electronic devices, and traditional EMP protection devices still have many problems in providing protection. In this paper, Infineon's ESD105-B1-02ELS and gas discharge tube are modelled and simulated, respectively, and their EMP protection characteristics are verified. The transient voltage suppressors have a small power capacity and an unsatisfactory protection effect, and the GDT has a larger power capacity but a long response time, so to combine the advantages and disadvantages of the two, this paper designs a pulse protection device consisting of TVS tubes and GDTs in parallel, with an insertion loss of less than 1 dB and a protection effect of more than 40 dB within 1–2 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of an EMC Stripline from DC to 400 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Based on the demands of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) measurements, a stripline for the tests of electromagnetic interference (EMI), electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS), etc. is designed and constructed in this work. Characteristic impedance of the proposed stripline is designed to be 50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$</tex>. In the simulated frequency range from DC to 500 MHz, the input VSWR is less than 1.2 and the insertion loss is less than 3.3 dB. Meanwhile, for 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}$</tex> input power, E-field strength in the testing area can reach a maximum of 73 V/m, and the field uniformity (FU) at most frequency points is less than 1 dB. The proposed stripline is processed and assembled, measured and simulated results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Research on Propagation Distance and Pattern of Vortex Radar Based on Uniform Circular Antenna Frequency Diverse Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper primarily introduces the vortex wave radar based on a circular frequency diverse antenna (FDA) array and analyzes the research on the propagation distance and patterns of vortex waves generated by the frequency diverse array. Through simulation and modeling of vortex wave patterns, we have successfully analyzed the dependency and variations of vortex beam patterns on propagation distance.

articleTitle: Electrically Large Complex Objects Recognition Using Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the shooting and bouncing ray method (SBR) is used to obtain electromagnetic (EM) scattering characteristics of electrically large complex objects, including different ships. Compared with finite integral time domain (FITD) and multi level fast multipole method (MLFMM), the SBR method are time and resource efficient. As a new type of machine learning algorithm, long short-term memory (LSTM) has unique advantages for dealing with sequential data like high resolution one-dimensional range profile (HRRP), since it can learn contextual relevance, simultaneously, solve long-term dependency problems with the help of a set of gate structures. Scattering characteristics database acquired by SBR is input into LSTM network to quickly recognize electrically large complex objects. It has better recognition performance than traditional support vector machine (SVM) and convolutional neural network (CNN) at different percentages of training data. This work will be helpful to neural networks implementations in quick recognition of electrically large complex objects.

articleTitle: A Multi-band Flexible Wearable Antenna Based on Split Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-band flexible wearable antenna based on split ring resonator is proposed based on the theory of microstrip antenna and the concept of metamaterial. In order to realize the flexible wearable and multi-band characteristics of the antenna, NF-30 flexible material is used as the substrate and the initial loop monopole antenna is deformed and designed. While introducing L-shaped branches on the ground plane, a coupling rectangular structure is introduced on the back of the antenna to enhance its radiation performance through proper adjustment of dimensions. The introduction of the split ring resonators alters the surface current distribution and radiation characteristics of the antenna. This has led to the emergence of two new operating frequency bands, reducing the antenna size and assisting in achieving miniaturization. The antenna can be operated in 6 bands: 2.07-2.65GHz, 3.71-3.98GHz, 4.21-4.33GHz, 5.48-6.33GHz, 7.58-8.19GHz and 8.63-9.67GHz. The bands above cover ISM, 3GPP, WI-MAX, Bluetooth, WIFI, WLAN (2.45GHz/5.8GHz), X-band, etc., and all have good impedance matching and radiation directionality. At the same time, the size of the antenna is only 50*50*1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In addition, the bending characteristics of the antenna and the influence of different parts of the human body on the antenna have been simulated and analyzed, and the return loss of the antenna and the conformal on the surface of human tissue are tested using a vector network analyzer. The test results are in good agreement with the simulation results, confirming its engineering significance and practicality.

articleTitle: The Electromagnetic Protection Design of Photoelectric System Based on Magnetic Material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper uses traditional magnetic material to realize the electromagnetic protection of the photoelectric system. Simulation results show that the traditional magnetic material loaded on the optical channel's inner wall can absorb electromagnetic waves, thus achieving electromagnetic protection. In the established circular and rectangular optical channels, the relative bandwidth of electromagnetic wave absorption can reach 112% and 97%, respectively. In addition, the absorption bandwidth increased from 97% to 125% by placing periodic metal rings on the magnetic material on the inner wall of the rectangular optical channel.

articleTitle: Microscopic Study on the Essence of Enamel Demineralization by Terahertz Near-Field Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Early demineralization of enamel has always been a concern for dentists, but revealing the essence of enamel demineralization from a microscopic perspective has been challenging due to the lack of appropriate detection methods. Terahertz technology, with its nondestructive and nonionizing properties, offers applications in biomedical imaging. In this study, we utilized continuous wave (CW) Terahertz near-field scanning microscope (THz-SNOM) technology to perform near-field imaging of enamel after demineralization. We examined the changes in surface structure and enamel permittivity during the demineralization process. The presented approach thus uncovers the mechanism of enamel demineralization from a microscopic perspective.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Holography Based on Diffractive Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In recent years, metasurface has demonstrated unprecedented capabilities in electromagnetic wave modulation and has achieved several results. In this work, we propose a two-layer metasurface structure, in which arbitrarily different holograms can be realized by rotating the first-layer metasurface, which greatly increases the reusability of the metasurface. Numerical simulation shows that our proposed metasurface structure can realize a multi-channel hologram, which has a wide range of applications in the fields of information encryption, information storage, etc.

articleTitle: Research on Cross-Device Bypass Attacks Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: SPECK algorithm is a typical lightweight algorithm with ARX structure, which is widely used in resource-constrained portable devices. In this paper, we address cross-device scenarios and explore the feasibility of accuracy as an index for evaluating the efficiency of attacks based on the bypass analysis of SPECK encryption algorithm. Three different scenarios are considered, i.e., different measurement locations for the same device, different IC sockets for the same chip, and different keys for different chips, to explore the impact of changes in the environment on the attack efficiency. The experiments show that using different devices and keys or changing chip IC sockets during the analysis and attack phases will seriously affect the accuracy metrics compared to changing the measurement locations of the probes. It is concluded that while accuracy is the most commonly used metric for monitoring and evaluating neural networks, it leads to a significant underestimation of the efficiency of attacks in cross-device conditions, and in fact models with low accuracy can still successfully attack the attacking device.

articleTitle: Simulation and Prediction of Vehicle EMC Radiation Performance Based on Near Field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The purpose of vehicle electromagnetic radiation emission measurement is to test the operating conditions of the vehicle to ensure that the external radiation generated by the vehicle does not affect the normal use of other surrounding electrical equipment. The perfect electromagnetic radiation emission simulation technology can effectively predict the radiation emission level of the vehicle in the vehicle development and design stage. Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to locate and obtain the interference source in the vehicle electromagnetic radiation emission simulation, this paper proposes a method combining near-field measurement and electromagnetic simulation to predict the EMC (electromagnetic compatibility) radiation performance of the whole vehicle. In this method, the near-field component on the main radiation plane around the disturbance source is measured by near-field scanning, which is imported into the electromagnetic simulation software FEKO as the excitation of the near-field equivalent radiation model, and the electromagnetic field distribution around the vehicle is simulated and calculated. This scheme provides a reference for the simulation and prediction of electromagnetic radiation emission of the whole vehicle, and also provides some help for the whole vehicle factory in troubleshooting the source of disturbance.

articleTitle: Directional Modulation Signal Generation Technology Based on Microwave Photonics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of slow scanning speed, small bandwidth, and high loss of traditional directional modulation, a directional modulation signal generation technology based on microwave photonics is proposed. By reasonably controlling the DC bias of the two modulators of the Dual-Parallel Mach-Zehnder Modulator (DPMZM), the directional modulation signal required by the antenna can be generated. The transmission and demodulation are simulated to evaluate the quality of the generated signals. The results show that the expected receiver successfully recovers the symbol information, and the signal-to-noise ratio reaches 25 dB. Meanwhile, the recovered symbol information is out of phase at the eavesdropping receiver, and the power is low. This shows that the system realizes the basic function of directional modulation.

articleTitle: A FDTD Lightning Return Stroke Model and its Application to Triggered-Lightning Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: FDTD method has been widely used in calculations of electromagnetic fields produced by a lightning return stroke and its effects on other systems. However, the traditional Pi-type distributed resistance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>) - inductance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>) - capacitance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>) model representing a lightning return stroke is no longer suitable for FDTD method. In this study, we propose a new type RLC model that consists of a current source at the lightning channel base feeding a series of passive RLC loads above. The model is then applied to two sets of channel base currents and multi-station electric field measurements from two return strokes in rocket-triggered lightning experiments. By fitting the simulated electric field with the measured electrical field at each station, an optimal set of lightning channel RLC values for each of the two return strokes were determined, and hence the current propagation speed and amplitude as a function of the channel height are successfully estimated. The results are well consistent with optical observations and physical model predictions.

articleTitle: Design of the fifth generation wireless terminal radiated spurious emission measurement system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With the development of the fifth generation (5G) wireless communication technology, 5G wireless terminals are widely used in various fields, and their radiated spurious emission have an increasingly significant impact on the electromagnetic environment. For the radiated spurious emission measurement system, it is necessary to meet the measurement requirements of both 5G wireless terminals and other wireless terminal devices, while also ensuring the efficiency and quality of measurement. This poses a great challenge to the radiated spurious emission measurement system, and it is necessary to redesign or upgrade the technology to achieve radiated spurious emission measurement of 5G wireless terminals. This article optimizes the design of a radiated spurious emission measurement system based on the working characteristics and measurement requirements of wireless terminal devices. The maximum frequency of measurement can reach 26.5GHz, achieving measurement of the second generation (2G), the third generation (3G), the four generation(4G), and 5G wireless terminals, as well as wireless local area networks (WLAN)and Bluetooth terminal devices.

articleTitle: Research on Simulation and Verification of Electromagnetic Radiation Characteristics of Spacecraft Assembly
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The spacecraft assembly mission cannot carry out effective Electromagnetic compatibility verification due to the constraints of large envelope of EMC test site, high test coverage and efficiency, and insufficient capability of dynamic condition verification. In order to solve the problem of simulation and verification of spacecraft assembly Electromagnetic compatibility, a combination-level evaluation method based on the prior data of electromagnetic radiation of modules is proposed in this paper, based on the electromagnetic field theory and Maxwell's equations derivation, the electromagnetic field radiated by a magnetic dipole at any point in space is obtained, and the electromagnetic radiation model of the component is reconstructed, to realize the prediction of electromagnetic radiation characteristics of composite body. The simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively support the prediction of electromagnetic radiation characteristics of cage-drawer integrated electronic equipment and spacecraft assembly.

articleTitle: A Novel Automatic Mesh Generation Technique for Curved Hexahedral
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for generating irregular curved hexahedral meshes from regular cuboid meshes. The algorithm utilizes cuboid to discretize the solid model, ignoring the inner and outer boundaries. Then, a special treatment process is applied to fit the boundary surfaces, generating high-quality irregular curved hexahedral discretized mesh. This algorithm is a novel raster method and is characterized by its simplicity, reliability, ease of programming, and high mesh quality.

articleTitle: Parametric Vector Fitting Applied to the Analysis of Arbitrary field-to-line coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, parametric vector fitting is applied to solve the coupling between arbitrary plane wave and circuit. The calculation results from full wave and parametric vector fitting on linear and nonlinear loads are compared. The validity of parametric vector fitting is verified by solving the response of an active circuit exposed to the irradiation of plane waves from different directions

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dipole Antenna with Band Rejection for Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A proposed multi-frequency dipole antenna with band rejection functionality is mainly composed of a positive and negative 45-degree crossed dipole and a reflector structure. The crossed dipole is fed by two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\ \Omega$</tex> coaxial cables to achieve ±45° polarized radiation over a wide bandwidth. The arms of the dipole are elliptical in shape, and they work together with the cross-shaped slot to generate two operating frequency bands. To achieve the band rejection performance of the antenna, the structure has been optimized, and a metal shield is used to ensure stable radiation patterns. Simulation results show that the antenna can radiate at around 3.5 GHz and 4.8 GHz within a frequency range that spans 32% of the center frequency. The band rejection is around 4.1 GHz. The VSWR within the radiation frequency range is less than 2, while the VSWR of the rejected band is greater than 5.5. In the radiation pattern of the antenna, the port isolation of the antenna is less than −20 dB for both ports. The antenna successfully achieved the bandwidth required for 5G base station operation under the conditions of the cross-shaped slot.

articleTitle: Preliminary Investigation on Human SAR Limits in Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This review describes the safety issues posed by human exposure to RF sites, mainly discussing the international standards related to human RF exposure limits and the differences between the standards. It also focuses on the existing studies on the testing of in-vehicle SAR values for different scenarios in view of the proliferation of electric vehicles at this stage, and finally arrives at the recommended standards for in-vehicle RF exposure limits to face increasingly complex electromagnetic exposure scenarios.

articleTitle: Improved One-Step Leapfrog CDI-FDTD Scheme with Excellent Numerical Dispersion Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: By intervening controlling parameters in the one-step leapfrog complying-divergence implicit (CDI) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, an improved scheme with excellent numerical dispersion performance is proposed. The proposal's computational accuracy and numerical dispersion are effectively improved while maintaining the unconditional stability property. Moreover, the effectiveness of improved low-dispersion one-step leapfrog CDI-FDTD scheme is demonstrated by simulations of the multiple-input multiple-output antenna element.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Damage Characteristics of Integrated Circuits with Various Pulse Width
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This research aims to propose an effective and low-cost solution for Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of integrated circuits, and comprehensively understand the impact of electrostatic discharge (ESD) on integrated circuits. The transient IV curves of integrated circuits were compared and analyzed. The transient conduction damage of integrated circuits under different pulse widths was studied. The results indicate that the comparison of transient IV curves and the characteristics of transient conduction damage have certain regularity.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic radiation safety of electric vehicle wireless charging system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The wireless charging technology of electric vehicles utilizes magnetic induction for energy transmission. Due to the use of non-direct contact methods, it can effectively avoid the drawbacks of exposed charging wires, and has obvious advantages in effectively promoting the intelligent process of vehicles. Therefore, it has received increasing attention. With the application of wireless charging technology, people have begun to pay attention to the impact of its electromagnetic radiation on the health of passengers and the public. On the other hand, with the improvement of medical level, the compatibility between wireless charging system and active implantable medical devices such as cardiac pacemakers, Cochlear implant has also attracted extensive attention. Firstly, this paper analyzes the existing wireless charging limits and testing method standards, and then takes a certain wireless charging system as an example to test the electric and magnetic field radiation values inside and outside the vehicle during wireless charging. By comparing with the standard limits, it can be concluded that the electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle model meets the standard.

articleTitle: A Large Frequency-Ratio Aperture-Shared Multi-Beam Transmit-Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an aperture-shared large frequency-ratio multi-beam transmit-array (TA) antenna working in the Sub-6GHz and millimeter-wave(mmW) bands. The TA antenna consists of an aperture-shared TA and a set of corresponding feeds. The mmW units is contained within the Sub-6GHz unit, and these two types of units barely affect each other's transmission performance. A prototype comprises three TAs has been fabricated and measured to verify the proposed design. The test results indicate that the beams of TA antenna can cover the range of ±28°, the mmW peak gain is up to 25.3 dBi at 24.5 GHz, and the Sub-6GHz peak gain is up to 13.2 dBi at 5.7 GHz. The overall bandwidth of mmW i.e.,|S11| < -10dB and the 3 dB gain bandwidth, is 22.5~26.5GHz, and that of the Sub-6GHz is 5.3~5.9GHz. For 5G wireless systems, the proposed multi-beam TA can be a good competitor.

articleTitle: Research on Propagation Properties in Buildings for Acoustically Actuated Monopole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The monopole antenna is a simple but powerful radio device that can be used to receive and transmit radio signals. In addition to its good performance for transmitting or receiving signals, electrically small metallic monopoles have common problems such as difficult impedance matching, large radiation loss and large volume. In this paper, an acoustically actuated monopole antenna (AAMA) is proposed to overcome the shortcomings of traditional metallic monopole methods, and promote the radiation efficiency, which can be used as a more compact radio transmitter. Moreover, the propagation properties of the AAMA is studied in reinforced concrete buildings and a maximum of communication distance of 26m is achieved. This kind of AAMA technology can be used in positioning/communication applications in blocked rooms and emergency situations.

articleTitle: High-resolution microwave photonic radar based on coherent fusion of time-coded LFM signal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A microwave photonic radar employing a time-coded linear frequency modulation signal is proposed, aiming to achieve high-range resolution detection while greatly enhancing anti-jamming capability. The time-coded linear frequency modulation signal is generated with microwave photonic multiplication technology, and then experiences microwave photonic de-chirping after being reflected by targets. Subsequently, coherent fusion processing is performed to the de-chirped signal and high range-resolution detection is achieved. Simulation results indicate that the proposed radar could provide a theoretical-level range resolution with a 6-band time-coded linear frequency modulation signal.

articleTitle: Design and Test of S-Band High Power Limiter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With electronic equipment to miniaturization, high-speed, integrated high-speed development, its electromagnetic sensitivity problems are increasingly prominent, and vulnerable to the impact of complex electromagnetic environment and damage. The limiter has the characteristics of small size, simple structure and strong limiter ability, which is widely used in all kinds of RF device protection. In order to enhance the power capacity of the limiter, this paper adopts the combination of TVS and PIN diodes to make a high-power limiter for S-band, which contains two-stage TVS, two-stage PIN diodes and one-stage Schottky diodes, in which microstrip inductors are added to optimize the multi-stage coordination. The test results show that the limiter insertion loss of 2.24dB at the design frequency point, can withstand 75dBm input power and provide 50dB isolation, both high-power capacity and strong limiting performance, the method can provide a reference for limiter power capacity expansion.

articleTitle: Response Analysis of Coupling Effect of Middle and Far-Field Nuclear Electromagnetic Pulse on Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The coupling effect of cables under the impact of middle and far-field nuclear electromagnetic pulse (NEMP) is studied. The induced current and voltage under the coupling effect of middle and far-field nuclear electromagnetic pulse are solved analytically by using the Agrawal model transmission line analysis method. In this paper, the image symmetry of the incident wave electric field with respect to the incident wave plane is discussed respectively, that is, when the electric field of incident wave is located on the left and right of the incident wave plane, the difference of the numerical analytical formula of the induced current at the load end. Through MATLAB software simulation, the effects of changing incident wave pitch and azimuth angle, cable load, cable length and cable height on terminal induced current are analyzed.

articleTitle: Developments and Trends of Directed Energy Technology in the United States
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Cyber-electromagnetic space has become another new area of operations after land, sea, air, and apace. As one of the cyber-electromagnetic offensive weapons, directed energy (DE) weapon has always been a hot topic in the frontier of national defense science and technology. DE is a focused beam of electromagnetic energy that is used to enable or create military effects, when used in conjunction with other military systems. With the development of science and technology, the increasing demand for offensive and defensive operations across the battle space, and the role of information in maintaining military parity across the battle space the military significance of DE is increasing day by day. Starting from the introduction of the characteristics of DE, this paper discusses the research and trend of directed energy weapon and put forward the enlightenment of the development.

articleTitle: A Fast Simulation Method in Range-Doppler Domain for Airborne Radar Clutter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The technology of clutter simulation is essential in radar design and electromagnetic environmental effects analysis. To meet the requirement for real-time simulation, a fast clutter simulation method for airborne radar is proposed in this paper. By simplifying the clutter model in range-Doppler domain, the dimension of the clutter simulation data is reduced. And a fast simulation method in range-Doppler domain is proposed. Compared with the traditional method, the computational complexity of the RD(Range-Doppler) method proposed in this paper is significantly decreased. The simulation results show that the RD method proposed in this paper has improved efficiency while ensuring simulation accuracy.

articleTitle: Implementation of a 50 W Power Amplifier for K-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, A solid-state power amplifier with high-power operating in the k-band is proposed. The power amplifier system uses the TGA4040 from QORVO as the chip and an 8-way waveguide power divider is implemented for power synthesis. In addition, the system is equipped with modules for bias control, power display, coupling detector and air-cooling protection. According to the experimental results, the amplifier system achieves a continuous wave saturation output power of more than 50W in the frequency range of 18-26.5GHz, a power gain of more than 47dB and a power additive efficiency (PAE) of around 20%, which meets the requirements of practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Influence of Orientation on Radiated Emission Measurement with the TEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: According to the IEC 61967–2, the Transverse Electromagnetic Mode(TEM) cell radiated emission test of integrated circuit(IC) should measure a printed circuit board (PCB) from four orientations, by turning the board over 90 degrees each time. In actual use, some engineers are unclear about the principle and purpose of the four orientations in this method, resulting in the inability to accurately understand the characteristics of the chip through the test results and flexibly tailor the standards according to their requirements. This paper analyzes the relationship between TEM cell radiated emission results and the orientations from three aspects: the principle of TEM cell measurement, the equivalent electrical dipole, and the coupling mechanism between IC current paths and TEM mode propagating. Then the test results from different orientations are verified and analyzed. Finally, suggestions are proposed for selecting orientations of TEM cell radiated emission measurement. The analysis of this paper has some guiding significance for the research and the measurement of IC electromagnetic compatibility(EMC).

articleTitle: A Novel Probe Selection Method for OTA Testing of 5G Massive MIMO Base Station on Static and Dynamic Channel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) testing technology has been applied to the millimeter wave massive multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) devices due to its advantages of simplicity and flexibility. The sectored multi-probe anechoic chamber (MPAC) is considered as the most promising method for massive MIMO base station OTA testing, but the performance of channel reconstruction in MPAC is restricted by probe arrangement and power weight. Due to the large number of probes, the cost of the sectored MPAC system is greatly increased. It is crucial to reduce the number of probes used while achieving high reconstruction accuracy. However, because of the high computational complexity, the probe selection methods suitable for the probe ring in two-dimensional MPAC are not applicable for sectored MPAC, especially for dynamic channels. This paper proposes a novel method to select the active probes for channel reconstruction. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, the root mean square error of the spatial correlation and power angular spectrum similarity percentage are used as the factors of merit. The static channel and dynamic channel are simulated respectively. The simulation results show that the novel algorithm can select the probes efficiently and achieve good reconstruction accuracy.

articleTitle: Ultralow-Loss Power Splitters Based on Shape Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: We demonstrate two kinds of low-loss 1 × 4 optical power splitters based on multimode interference (MMI) couplers. By using the adjoint shape optimization method, the shapes of MMI couples are optimized to realize uniform power splitting and a splitting ratio of 1:2:4:8. Simulation results show that the insertion losses at the wavelength of 1550 nm are 0.04 dB and 0.17 dB for 1 × 4 uniform power splitter and 1:2:4:8 power splitter, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Millimeter-Wave Low Cross-Polarization Miniaturized Antenna Measurement System Based on Beam Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a design method of a miniaturized antenna measurement system (MAMS) with low cross-polarization in millimeter-wave band. In this design method, the cause of cross-polarization in the tri-reflector system is analyzed first by using the beam mode theory. Then the geometric structure of the system is determined by using the cross-polarization elimination condition. Furthermore, a MAMS with main aperture size of 0.6 m, feed rotation angle of 30° and the overall structure size of 1.85 m ×0.6 m ×2.16 m is finally realized. The numerical simulation results show that the cross-polarization of the system is less than −40 dB, and the co-polarization amplitude (phase) ripple is within 1 dB (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>) in the frequency range of 100–300 GHz. In addition, the diameter of the quiet zone (QZ) is 0.42 m, and the utilization rate of the QZ can reach over 70%. This design method provides a theoretical reference for the design and construction of a miniaturized high performance antenna measuring instrument with flexibility and mobility.

articleTitle: Multi-Domain Feature Fusion Based Radar Deception Jamming Recognition Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Considering the challenges posed by low recognition probability, high computational complexity, and difficult engineering implementation in radar deception jamming recognition under a low jamming-to-noise ratio (JNR), a method for recognizing radar deception jamming based on multi-domain feature fusion is proposed. This method analyzes the mathematical models of three types of deception jamming-intermittent sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ), dense false target jamming (DFTJ), and distance deception jamming (DDJ) -to extract two features: envelope fluctuation and waveform similarity in the time and frequency domains, respectively. Jamming classification and recognition are achieved using a multi-class support vector machine (multi-class SVM) model. Simulation results demonstrate that as JNR increases, there is a gradual improvement in the recognition rate which reaches 90%at ldB.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic Interference Risk of Vehicle to Active Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Active implantable medical devices such as cardiac pacemakers belong to three types of high-risk equipment, which should be tested for electromagnetic compatibility according to the requirements of engineering doctors. However, patients wearing such devices will appear in all kinds of life scenarios, and the electromagnetic compatibility requirements of vehicles are far higher than the requirements of engineering doctors. Therefore, this paper first analyzes the electromagnetic interference immunity performance of active implantable medical devices, then introduces the potential electromagnetic interference factors of road vehicles, and finally analyzes the electromagnetic interference risk of active implantable medical devices by collecting the electromagnetic radiation data of vehicles in different states and different positions. The results showed that: The magnetic field radiation value of the electric drive system of the sample vehicle is far lower than the interference immunity level requirements of active implantable medical devices, but the radiation level of the vehicular wireless charging module has approached or even exceeded the interference immunity requirements, especially with the increase of the transmission power of the wireless charging module. Patients wearing the device should keep a certain distance from the wireless charging module to ensure that it is free from interference.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Risk in Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With the application of 5G communication technology in the vertical industry, the electromagnetic interference and compatibility issues between newly introduced wireless communication devices and various electronic and electrical equipment that originally existed in the vertical industry have become increasingly important. Taking the nuclear power industry as an example, the application of wireless communication technology in the nuclear power plant area may cause harmful interference to electronic and electrical equipment originally used for power generation or other purposes in the factory area, leading to shutdown or other serious safety accidents. This article mainly studies the analysis and evaluation methods of electromagnetic risks that may arise after the introduction of wireless communication technology in nuclear power plants, in order to quickly analyze and locate the electromagnetic risks and risk levels that may arise during the construction of wireless communication networks in the nuclear power plant area, and improve the efficiency of 5G communication network construction in the nuclear power plant area.

articleTitle: Analysis and Experimental Validation of the Influencing Factors of UAVs to Power Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With the increasing civilian use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), their impact on public safety is receiving increasing attention from society. This article focuses on analyzing the influencing factors of different types of civil UAVs to power substations. Establishing a security threat assessment system for different types of civilian UAVs on primary and secondary equipment in power substations is a crucial step toward preventing any potential damage caused by UAVs. By conducting experiments to measure the performance of UAVs and their impact on the electromagnetic interference of the secondary equipment in power substations, the article provides valuable perspectives into the potential risks posed by UAVs. The results of the experiments suggest that the impact of UAVs on the primary equipment of power substations is greater than their electromagnetic interference on the secondary equipment. This finding could help guide future efforts to prevent the impact of civilian UAVs on power substations.

articleTitle: A calibration apparatus for high-power radio frequency pulse sensors based on hydrothermal methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A pulse power sensor with a peak power of 35kW is an essential component in the production of advanced nuclear magnetic resonance equipment. However, the traceability of its measured values remains a challenging issue. The conventional approach involves using cascade-coupled methods for traceability, but the calibration of couplers and attenuators is typically performed under continuous low power conditions. This method fails to ensure consistent parameter performance under high-power pulse signals, resulting in significant uncertainty in traceability results. In this study, a hydrothermal methodology is employed for the traceability of high-power radio frequency pulses. The average power of the radio frequency pulse signal is directly traced back to a low-frequency alternating power source, while also measuring the pulse signal duty cycle using an oscilloscope. This approach aligns with the measurement principles of national power standards, thereby offering higher measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Antenna Test Range System Based on Dual-polarization Metamaterial Lens
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a new metamaterial lens antenna for the compact antenna test range (CATR) system is proposed. In this CATR system design, the feed source is a choke coil horn antenna, and the lens unit is formed by etching a slotted metal sheet on a single-layer dielectric substrate. The size of the unit is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\text{mm}\times 5\text{mm}$</tex>, and the overall lens size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$53\text{cm}\times 53\text{cm}$</tex>, the number of lens units is 101×101. The simulation result shows that at the frequency of 26GHz, when the peak-to-peak field amplitude is less than 1.6dB and the peak-to-peak phase is less than 10°, a 21cm quiet zone (QZ) is formed at a distance of 1.8m from the feed. The aperture utilization efficiency is 40%, which indicates that the CATR system achieves a high-quality, large-area, dual-polarization QZ performance using only one single-layer metamaterial lens.

articleTitle: Microwave Photonic-Based High-Speed Target Detection Using Hyperbolic Frequency Modulation Wave
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Hyperbolic frequency modulation wave (HFM) is used for high-speed target detection in wideband radar due to its immunity to doppler dispersion. Traditional wideband HFM receiving method suffers from limited analog-to-digital converter bandwidth. This paper presents a microwave photonic (MWP)-based method to achieve wideband HFM receiving, where a swept laser is used for wideband HFM compression. Experiments show that high-resolution ranging and ISAR imaging of high-speed target based on HFM is achieved, with 1D resolution of 3.97cm and 2D resolution of 4.07cm*4.41cm.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Power Integrated Circuits Using Finite Element Method with Hybrid Mesh
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a fast calculation method for on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\mathrm{I})\mathrm{S}(\text{on})})$</tex> of power integrated circuits based on finite element method with hybrid mesh is proposed. Specifically, for the power devices with irregular internal structures, a hybrid triangular mesh is employed to discretize the models. Then, a Laplace equivalent conductance matrix based on the mesh nodes is established, and solved for resistor network. The proposed method is compared with the conventional rectangular mesh approach, and the result show that the proposed one significantly optimizes the number of mesh nodes under the same accuracy of resistance values.

articleTitle: A CRLH-TL based dual-band compact antenna for smart grid 5G terminal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A CRLH-TL based dual-band compact antenna was designed and implemented. The proposed antenna with compact volume at 42.5mm × 30mm × 1.4mm achieved 700MHz-750MHz zeroth-order resonance band and 1900MHz-2800MHz wide impedance band. The proposed antenna can be applied in 5G wireless devices in smart grid scenario.

articleTitle: A Wideband 1-Bit Reflectarray Antenna using Magneto-Electric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A wideband reflectarray antenna (RA) using magneto-electric resonator and 1-bit phase quantization beam-steering ability is presented in this paper. The unit cell is capable of switching between magnetic resonance and electric resonance states by manipulating the on-off states of the PIN diodes, enabling 1-bit reflection phase switching. The phase bandwidth achieved in simulations spans from 11.87 GHz to 22.74 GHz (62.8%). The proposed unit cell is applied to design a 16 × 16 units reflectarray antenna, and the simulations demonstrate excellent bandwidth and radiation pattern performance. The reflectarray antenna exhibits a peak gain of 21.7 dBi, 1dB bandwidth is 13.7 GHz-19.1 GHz (32.9%), and 3dB bandwidth is 12.3 GHz-20.6 GHz (50.4%). These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed magneto-electric resonator mechanism for realizing wideband reflectarray antennas with precise beam steering capabilities.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Broadband IC-Stripline Cell Radiation Emission
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With the continuous improvement of chip integration, the problem of integrated circuit (IC) electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is becoming more and more prominent. The continuous improvement of the working frequency of ICs requires a wider band of IC-EMC measurement equipment. IC-Stripline cell is important measurement equipment in the field of IC-EMC. And in recent years, several new types of broadband IC-Stripline cells have emerged, such as standard IC-Stripline cell, dielectric IC-Stripline cell and slotted septum IC-Stripline cell. Based on standards, the paper compares the radiation emission test results of three types IC-Stripline cells and analyzes the reasons for test errors.

articleTitle: Influence of Quadratic Gradient Boundary on Cable Fault Location based on Impedance Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: When applying integral transform to analyze impedance spectrum to locate latent faults in cable, the influence of fault boundary on location results is not fully considered, which may affect the feasibility of field application. In this paper, simulation research is conducted to explore how a nonlinear quadratic gradient boundary influences the fault location result when applying integral transform to analyze impedance spectrum. The conclusion drawn from this research can be an important supplement to the application of integral transform method to locate potential faults in power cable.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of a High-Efficiency Vertical Polarization Splitting Grating Coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Herein, a high-efficiency vertical polarization splitting grating coupler (PSGC) is demonstrated using inverse design method. The insertion loss for LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>and LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sup> modes of this PSGC is minimized to −1.52 dB and −1.62 dB at 1555 nm.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Compensation Scheme for Adaptive Variable Step Digital Backward Propagation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a nonlinear damage compensation scheme of adaptive variable step size digital back propagation (DBP) algorithm is proposed, which is based on the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to iteratively compute the nonlinear coefficient and the step size influence factor at the same time. This scheme improves the nonlinear compensation capability of the DBP and the nonlinear compensation is improved by 2.3% compared with the traditional DBP.

articleTitle: A DC-to-18 GHz 6-bit CMOS Digital Step Attenuator with Low Phase Error and Compact Size
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a DC-to-18 GHz low phase error 6-bit digitally controlled attenuator fabricated in CMOS 55nm process is proposed. The proposed attenuator utilizes a phase-compensated structure to minimize the phase difference between the reference state and the attenuation state, resulting in a low root mean square (RMS) phase error. Additionally, the cascading method of the attenuation units is optimized to ensure accurate attenuation across a wide range. Experimental measurements demonstrate that the designed digital attenuator achieves a maximum RMS phase error of less than 4° within the operating frequency band. It offers an attenuation range of 31.5 dB with a step size of 0.5 dB. Remarkably, the core area, excluding the pad, occupies a small area of 0.015 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Improved Adaptive Digital Back Propagation Algorithm Based On Adam Algorithm For Fiber Nonlinear Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an Adam-DBP algorithm is proposed for the digital signal processing part of the optical receiver. The algorithm is based on the DBP algorithm, with the addition of the Adam algorithm so that it has the ability to adaptively compensate for the signal, overcoming the shortcomings of the traditional DBP algorithm with poor flexibility, and compared with other optimization algorithms, it has a faster iteration speed and reduces the complexity of the system.

articleTitle: An Array Element with Reconfigurable Phase Center
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A phase center reconfigurable array element with the same aperture and fixed physical shape is proposed. An asymmetric field distribution model is introduced and the influence of different phase center positions on the aperture efficiency is analyzed.
