When the phase center is reconstructed near the physical center, the element aperture efficiency is higher than that of the traditional sparse array. Taking multi-mode circular patch as an example, the far-field distribution of the multi-mode patch is derived, and the relationship between the phase center position and the power ratio of two modes is given. A full-wave simulation model is established to verify the reconfigurable position of the phase center. The simulation results are in good agreement with the theoretical results, and the phase center is reconstructed to ±6mm of the physical center.

articleTitle: Coupling Analysis of Grounding Wires of Vehicle Equipment in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The grounding wire of electric vehicle equipment is an important part of the electric connection between electrical equipment and electric vehicle, which not only ensures the safety of equipment, but also reduces the risk of electric shock. At the same time, the grounding wire has also become an important path of electromagnetic interference coupling between vehicle equipment. In this paper, by analyzing the disturbance mechanism caused by the grounding wire of vehicle equipment, the coupling model of the grounding wire of electric vehicle is built, and the transmission coupling of the grounding wire is analyzed, and the correctness of the model is verified by the method of experimental verification. Based on the analysis results, the conditions that should be met for the position of the grounding wires of the vehicle driving dynamic controller (VDC) equipment to ensure the normal operation of the VDC are obtained.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic Compatibility of Fuel Cell System Components
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In order to study the mutual interference between fuel cell's components and improve anti-interference ability of sensitive components, a test system for DC/DC converter, Air Compressor Controller (ACC), and FCU controller is established, and radiation emission measurements is conducted. Then, measurement results of DC/DC converter and ACC were used as interference sources, and a simulation model was established. The interference current signals on the DC/DC converter and ACC cables were collected as excitation sources for the simulation model. The impact of two components on the FCU controller was studied. The results showed that the coupling current on the FCU controller cable could exceed 100mA and limit. In addition, the simulation model was used to study the radiation anti-interference characteristics of the FCU controller after adding a cable shielding layer. Under the plane wave interference of 25V/m~100V/m, the induced current on the FCU controller cable was small, which will not affect the normal operation of the FCU controller.

articleTitle: Equivalent Modeling of the Radiation of Microwave Circuits with Irregular Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Modeling and analyzing radio-frequency interference of microwave circuits is a challenge task due to increasingly high integration density and surrounding complex environment. In this paper, an efficient equivalent modeling method of microwave circuits with irregular ground plane is proposed and verified. Radiated fields above and below the ground plane can be accurately evaluated with superior efficiency compared to full-wave numerical methods. This method provides a promising candidate for solving radio-frequency interference problems of microwave circuits.

articleTitle: Design and Application of EMI Filter Between Multi-Servo Systems Under Unified Power Supply and Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Due to the different power supply necessity and operating characteristics, the horizontal landing vehicle's multi-electromechanical servo system generates electromagnetic interference (EMI) between the systems under the unified power supply and distribution system, resulting in abnormal of signals such as sampling and detection, and even affecting the operation of the entire system. In order to solve the electromagnetic compatibility problem between the multi-electromechanical servo systems, the principle of interference generation and the method of suppression is introduced, and the transmission path of the interference in an example is explained. A design of two sets of multi-stage EMI filters between the systems is proposed. According to the working characteristics of the interference source servo system, the filter grounding capacitance is added based on the original filter. The value of the capacitance is clarified through theoretical calculation and test, then the result shows that the interference between the systems is eliminated. The effectiveness of the filter design and the feasibility of application are clearly verified.

articleTitle: An Innovative Multi-Mode Detection Method for Vortex Electromagnetic Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Mode detection of orbital angular momentum (OAM) has become a hot research topic as an important procedure for vortex electromagnetic wave applications. In this paper, A novel mode detection method based on optimized dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) is proposed. Dimension reduction is used to obtain spiral term information of vortex electromagnetic waves. The results demonstrate that this method can not only detect single-mode but also realize accurate and efficient multi-mode detection in coaxial multiplexing transmission scenarios. Considering the divergence effect, the mode detection of partial reception is further discussed in order to realize the effective transmission of vortex electromagnetic waves over long distances.

articleTitle: Algebraic Fault Analysis of GIFT_64_128 Block Cipher Based on Hardware Trojan
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Based on the algebraic fault analysis method, a new hardware trojan is proposed to implement fault injection of cryptographic chip on FPGA. A random state value is used to realize the activation circuit and a single XOR-gate is used to realize the bit-flipping at a specific position. Set up a variety of random state sequences to achieve multiple single-bit fault injections. According to the algebraic properties of the GIFT_64_128 block cipher, using the algebraic fault analysis method, the key can be solved by at least 12 single-bit faults based on the fault ciphertexts and incorrect encryption information generated by the faults. The number of faults required is significantly reduced compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Standard antenna measurement for mobile communication based on the three-antenna extrapolation technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: To achieve the uncertainty requirement of 0.25dB for antenna gain measurement in the communication industry standard (YD/T 2868–2020), the three-antenna extrapolation technique is used to measure the standard antenna employed in the mobile communication base station measurement, and for comparison the traditional reference antenna method is also implemented. The measurement results of the two methods are compared, and the uncertainty of the gain is evaluated. It indicates that using the three-antenna extrapolation technique can achieve a 0.2dB uncertainty for the standard antenna in this case. The measurement analysis provides an usefull example for the measurements of similar antennas.

articleTitle: Recent Advances on High-Frequency Computational Electromagnetic Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this work, high-frequency computational electromagnetic methods including the multilevel fast physical optics (MLFPO) method and iterative physical optics (IPO) method based on quadratic patches are proposed to accelerate the calculation of physical optics (PO) integral of electrically large target and enhance computational accuracy of target with multiple scattering effects. In actual scenario, targets are located at the near zone of radar, thus the near-field linear-amplitude based fast physical optics method (LFPO) is presented to describe radiation features of target. To compensate for the lack of these PO-based methods in neglecting the contribution of currents in the dark region of target, the incremental length of diffraction coefficient (ILDC) method based on shadow boundary is proposed to solve the diffracted field of creeping wave. Moreover, a parametric scattering center model based on stationary phase method (SPM) is discussed to analyze scattering features of complex target. Efficiency and accuracy of these methods are verified via numerical examples. Presented computational electromagnetic methods are of great significance to the analysis of high-frequency electromagnetic characteristics.

articleTitle: The Influence of Temperature on the Electromagnetic Leakage in Side Channel Attack Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of temperature on the quality of electromagnetic leakage signals in the context of deep learning-based attacks. The Simeck32/64 algorithm is employed as a case study to exemplify this phenomenon. The proposed methodology involves training a deep learning model to perform attacks on electromagnetic leakage signals collected at three distinct temperature levels: −20°C, 20°C, and 60°C. The experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves optimal attack performance under a low-temperature scenario, exhibiting a test accuracy of 100% and successfully compromising all 64-bit keys of the Simeck32/64 algorithm. However, as the temperature increases, the model's attack success rate diminishes significantly, yielding test accuracies of 94.5% and 74.5% in normal and high-temperature scenarios, respectively.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Ground Wire Voltages Along Transmission Line Under Lightning Strikes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Harvesting power from ground wires is a promising solution for the power supply problem of online monitoring device on the overhead transmission lines. Nevertheless, this method is more likely to suffer lightning overvoltage or overcurrent due to the position of power harvesting device. In order to promote the reliability of harvesting power from ground wires, this paper studies the ground wire voltages under different lightning strike situations with different ground wire connection methods. Meanwhile, the influence of lightning current waveform, span and tower impulse resistance is also studied in this paper. The results of this paper can guide the design of overvoltage protection module of the power harvesting device on the ground wire.

articleTitle: Properly Normalized RCS Under a Tapered Incident Wave for Rough Surface Scattering Using SSA Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Two different explicit formulations of incident power are proposed to calculate the normalized radar cross section (RCS) scattering from the ocean-like surfaces illuminated by a tapered wave. The tapered wave is applied to circumvent artificial reflections from the edges of illuminated finite surface. Explicit formulations of incident power are derived by using two different types of Poynting vectors. The scattering field can be calculated by the first-order small slope approximation (SSA-I) method. The resulting normalized RCS analysis are demonstrated to verify the validity of the proposed method, compared with the experimental results.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on a Spiral-Shaped SIW
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A high-gain circularly polarized (CP) leaky wave antenna (LWA) is proposed in this manuscript, which composes a set of slots printed on a spiral-shaped substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). The high gain is able to achieved by the long traveling-wave path of the spiral-shaped SIW. The impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is from 9.7 GHz to 10.5 GHz with| S11| less than −10 dB. And the peak gain of the proposed antenna can reach 13.2 dB. It offers advantages of compact structure, low production cost, and high gain.

articleTitle: A Novel Calibration Method of Quasi-Peak Detector for EMI Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: According to the present version of CISPR16-1-1, a pulse generator with a uniform spectrum is used to calibrate the quasi-peak detector. The issues in the pulse generator calibration method are discussed. Then this paper presents a novel calibration method of quasi-peak detector based on pulse-modulated carriers. Finally, several examples are provided to verify the feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: Non-linear and damage effect on low noise amplifier injected by high power microwave
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Taking the SPF5043Z low noise amplifier of a certain type of UAV's data link as the research object, a low noise amplifier circuit is designed, and effect experiment platform of the low noise amplifier injected by high power microwave is constructed, and the effect experiments are carried out. The changes in output power and gain of the low noise amplifier with input power are clarified, and the pulse width and repetition frequency of high power microwave on the damage threshold of the low noise amplifier are studied, which provides technical support for the analysis of the damage effect mechanism and protection reinforcement of the data link.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Influence of Different Stirrers on Performance of Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Various stirrers have been developed for reverberation chamber (RC) to meet kinds of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) test and Over-The-Air (OTA) test. We designed 3 types of stirrer paddles for 4 same dimension RCs. Chamber validation with the same working volumes for the 4 RCs were performed. The field uniformity results presented that stirrers with rotationally symmetrical structures would decrease the performance of RC. Chamber decay times were also measured and compared.

articleTitle: Common Mode Noise Analysis inside the Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In order to model the common mode (CM) noise source inside the integrated circuit (IC), many circuits combing real tests have been proven effective. However, the accuracy of the extract method from the test to the model is a key problem that limits the application of the inside source. In this paper, a smart transfer circuit has been developed to extract the common mode source. The results show that this method can recover the source wave very accurate. Meanwhile, using the CM source, we can forecast the 3M RE result from the PCB trace radiation.

articleTitle: Wavelength Extension of Optical Signals Based on Cascaded Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Wavelength extension of optical signals plays an important role in optical computation and optical signal processing. In this paper, a wavelength extension architecture based on MZM and PM cascade is proposed to realize configurable wavelength extension of optical signals and form optical homologous copies at dozens of different wavelengths. In the simulation, the wavelength extension achieves the extended spectrum with 39 flat beams, the flat beams account for 37.86% of the total beams, and the flatness reaches 1.05dB.

articleTitle: Accelerate Electromagnetic Scattering Computation with LSTM Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces an approach called Electromagnetic Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network (EM-LSTMNN) for accelerating Radar Cross-Section (RCS) computations in the optimization of low RCS for large-sized electric targets. The proposed method converts the conventional electromagnetic numerical calculation into an efficient numerical calculation using the LSTM neural network, resulting in a significant improvement in RCS computation speed. To assess the effectiveness of this approach, a downscaled model of a large-sized ship is employed as the target for low RCS optimization. Each modification made to the target's mesh data during the optimization process is stored in the dataset as a new element. As the ship scaling model undergoes modifications during the optimization process, the new mesh data is recorded, thus adding a new element to the dataset at each time step. This forms a time series representation of the mesh model. By utilizing the dataset collected throughout the optimization process, the proposed EM-LSTMNN model is trained using data-driven approaches, with a training time of approximately 106 seconds. It is worth noting that this training time is significantly smaller compared to existing methods that employ fully connected neural networks. The performance of the proposed approach is demonstrated by comparing the RCS calculation results obtained through this method with those obtained through traditional electromagnetic simulations.

articleTitle: A Field Trial of Broadband Photonic Beam Processor Based on Space-Time-Frequency Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we perform a field trial test of a photonic-based full K-band phased array radar system demonstrator in a real scenario. The actual implementation of the system employs the broadband photonic beam processor as the receiver which has been previously verified enabling the all-optical multifunction integrated receive. The feasibility in practical applications is further proved by the experimental results with observation of the non-cooperative target inside the beam region, i.e. a moving unmanned aerial vehicle in practice here.

articleTitle: Discussion on Networking Requirements and Testing Methods of Remote Laparoscopy Surgery Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Remote Laparoscopy surgery robots can help doctors achieve accurate and personalized surgery, and improve the quality of surgery to a certain extent. At the same time, remote application alleviates the problem of uneven medical resources. The application of remote Laparoscopy surgical robots is related to the life safety and data safety of patients, but there are no standards for technical requirements and testing methods related to its remote applications. This paper starts with the network requirements of the remote Laparoscopy robot, studies its test environment and test content, and provides a reference for the healthy development of remote Laparoscopy surgical robot industry.

articleTitle: Design of Single-Layer Millimeter Wave Broadband Dual-Polarization Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A wideband dual-polarization reflectarray unit is proposed in this paper, which is applied to broadband reflectarray antenna. This unit has parallel and equidistant phases in the range of 24-27GHz, flat slope and good reflection performance. The simulation results show that the gain of the antenna designed with this unit is greater than 29.5dBi at 24-29GHz, and the wideband performance is realized, and the 3dB gain bandwidth is 18.9%.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Transient in Secondary Cable above a Grounding Grid under a Lightning Strike
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: When a lightning strikes a substation, transient disturbance will affect the secondary cable on the grounding grid through the uneven ground potential distribution and the mutual inductance between the cable and the ground grid. In this paper, a numerical method to calculate the transient disturbance in the secondary cable is presented. Based on the method of moments, a circuit model of grounding grid is developed taking into consideration the mutual inductance between the secondary cable and the ground conductor, while a transmission line model of the secondary cable is established with the consideration of uneven ground potential distribution and the mutual inductance between the secondary cable and the ground conductor. Then, the two models are unified. Simulation results show that the mutual inductance between the double end grounded cable and the grounding conductors greatly affects the transient disturbance in secondary cable. While the uneven potential distribution mainly affects that by forming a potential difference between both ends of the cable and the ground grid.

articleTitle: Mmwave radar and vision fusion for semantic 3D reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: 3D reconstructed point clouds have been widely used in the fields of autonomous driving, smart city, map mapping, etc. Semantic segmentation of 3D models has also received wide attention as an important method for environment perception. This paper presents a 3D point cloud segmentation approach that fuses millimeter wave radar and vision. Firstly, by scanning and reconstructing the same scene separately using millimeter-wave radar and the camera, we obtain radar point clouds and visual reconstruction point clouds. The radar point cloud is projected onto the Multi-View images so that the pixel points carry millimeter wave radar reflection intensity values. Then, 2D image segmentation is performed on the Multi-View images to assign semantic labels to each pixel point. Finally, labels are assigned to 3D point cloud by employing a probability-based semantic fusion method. The final generated dense 3D point cloud model contains color, spatial location, electromagnetic wave reflection intensity, and semantic label. The method can accurately segment small and mediumsized outdoor scenes, and can effectively distinguish objects with similar appearances but different materials.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metasurface with Varactor Diodes for Generation of Multi-mode OAM Vortex Beams
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a reconfigurable metasurface that can generate multi-mode OAM vortex beams with high purity in the X-band. The metasurface has two-dimensional reconfigurable properties and can realize arbitrary phase distributions. Then, by encoding the phase distribution of the meta-atoms, various OAM vortex beams including +1, +2, and +3 orders are generated, where the purity of all modes can be above 70%. As a validation, the metasurface composed of 30×30 meta-atoms is fabricated and measured. Both simulation and measurement results demonstrate the capability of the proposed metasurface to generate multi-mode OAM beams with high purity, indicating the application potentials of proposed meta-devices in future OAM communications.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Two Ground Grid Potentials after a Triggered Lightning Stroke
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: It has been determined that the discharge of lightning current to ground through grounding grid results in high potential at the grounding grid and other nearby grounding grids, which is very destructive. In the present paper, based on artificial lightning trigger technology, the characteristics of the ground potential rise (GPR), the transient effect at the active grid under the transient impulse of lightning current was analyzed. The impulse ground resistance is found to decrease for large input currents, On the other hand, for small input currents it usually increases. In addition, the characteristics of the transfer potential of the passive grid which is located 40 m from the active grid were analyzed, and it was shown that the peak value of the transfer potential at the passive grid was approximately 5.1% of the peak value of the ground potential at the active grid during the return stroke. The achievements made in this study may contribute toward the optimization of the simulation model.

articleTitle: An Efficient Discontinuous-Galerkin Integral Method for Coaxial Cable Feeding Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Using coaxial cables for feeding antennas or connecting different microwave components is ubiquitous in modern microwave engineering, and the method of moments (MoM) based on integral equations is a versatile approach for accurate simulation. This paper presents a novel and efficient scheme for coaxial cable structures. To avoid extremely fine mesh for the long-thin inner conductor surface of the coaxial cable, the wire model neglecting circumferential components of currents is adopted. In addition, the discontinuous Galerkin integral equation (DGIE) scheme is developed so that conformal mesh surface-wire mesh is no longer necessary. Representative numerical examples, including a shorted-circuit coaxial cable waveguide and a coaxial cable-fed monopole antenna, are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High-net-gain erbium-doped hybrid waveguide amplifiers on chalcogenide photonic platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Chalcogenide glasses (ChGs) have been widely used in integrated photonics due to their excellent properties of low loss and high nonlinearity. However, the performance of the active waveguide amplifiers is merely adequate. Here, a hybrid waveguide amplifier in Ge25Sb10S65 planar waveguide by a highly erbium-doped Al2O3 layer is demonstrated. High-quality Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>: Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin film with high concentration of 9×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> is fabricated by atomic layer deposition technique. And the GeSbS waveguide is manufactured by thermal evaporation and plasma etching. Signal enhancement up to 11.93 ± 0.3 dB and internal net gain of approximately 1.28 dB/cm are obtained at 1533 nm in the 1.5-cm-long and 0.8-cm-long waveguides upon 1480 nm pumping, respectively. The hybrid configuration is proved to be an efficient strategy to implement ChG-based integrated waveguide amplifiers.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Airborne P-Static Discharge Parameter Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: P-Static discharge interference protection verification testing plays a critical role in the airworthiness certification flight tests for civil aircraft. However, the testing phase faces challenges due to the lack of reliable measurement methods for static discharge parameters, which impairs the accurate determination of whether the aircraft is in a static discharge environment, consequently impacting the evaluation of the test results. To tackle this issue, a specialized Airborne P-Static discharge parameter measurement system was designed based on the characteristics of aircraft static discharge. The experimentation revealed that each discharge of the static discharger comprises a pulse train consisting of six pulses with varying amplitudes, lasting approximately 290ns. The time intervals between adjacent pulses are consistent. The pulse amplitudes gradually decay, with no discernible pattern or rule for the decay rate. Additionally, the experiment also identified variations in the duration of the pulse data in the radiation field across different locations. The spectrum data analysis indicated that the radiation energy primarily concentrates below 200MHz, with stable peaks observed at multiple frequency points. The maximum peak amplitude recorded is 50dBm. The study results demonstrate the effectiveness of the Airborne P-Static discharge parameter measurement system. This system facilitates the measurement of key parameters during the electrostatic discharge process, thus providing crucial experimental data for a comprehensive investigation of electrostatic discharge phenomena and their associated interference effects.

articleTitle: Low-Pass Filtering Cable Design Utilizing Defected Conductor Layer with Pi-Shaped Defected Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Insulated electrical wires coated with a specific defected conductor layer exhibit filtering advantages, making them suitable for reducing electromagnetic interference conducted by cables in complex electromagnetic environments. The etched-out pattern on the defected conductor layer serves as a distributed filtering circuit, equivalent to a lumped circuit added to the transmission line circuit of the cable. In this paper, we present a low-pass filtering cable designed using a defected conductor layer with five cascaded Pi-shaped resonators. The defected conductor layer is fabricated on a polyimide film substrate, and simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the designed low-pass filtering cable exhibits a sharp transition band and an ultra-wide stopband, effectively achieving its filtering function.

articleTitle: A Performance Test Method for Medical Ultrasound Remote Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Ultrasound robot is the integration of ultrasound imaging equipment and robot system, which assists doctors to obtain high-quality ultrasound images for examination and diagnosis. With the continuous progress of communication technology, especially 5G network communication, ultrasound robots break the limit of distance in ultrasound examination in the past, realize the separation of doctors and patients, and create a new way of ultrasound diagnosis. This paper reviews the application scenarios and examples of ultrasonic robot, analyzes the system model, key technology and network performance indicators of remote ultrasonic robot, aiming to build a test environment and clarify the technical requirements and test methods of remote ultrasonic diagnosis system. It is conducive to ensuring the safety and effectiveness of equipment function and performance and improving the efficiency and quality of remote treatment.

articleTitle: Coupled Analysis of Electromagnetic and Thermal Fields of Vivaldi Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With the advancement of integrated circuit technology, antennas have become increasingly miniaturized and integrated. However, the electromagnetic thermal effects arising from dielectric losses in materials can no longer be ignored. Therefore, it is imperative to conduct electromagnetic-thermal analysis of microstrip antennas. This paper utilizes the finite element numerical method for the integrated analysis of the electromagnetic-thermal effects in Vivaldi antennas.

articleTitle: Analysis of Interference on FMCW Radar Velocity Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With the rise of autonomous driving technology in recent years, millimeter wave radar has been more and more widely used in automobiles. In complex actual road conditions, the mutual interference between a large number of vehicle-mounted FMCW radars working in the same frequency band, as well as the existence of some human intentional or unintentional interference in special scenarios may make the target detection error. In this paper, based on the working mechanism of FMCW radar, the influence process of interference on the speed detection results is deduced, and a generalized interference analysis platform is proposed to do quantitative calculations on the influence of interference signals of different frequencies and intensities on speed detection. Through the research of this paper can be more in-depth understanding of the role of interference on the target judgment mechanism, for radar anti-jamming algorithm and target judgment algorithm research to provide reference basis.

articleTitle: Flexible Setups Based on a Novel Probe Selection Method for MIMO OTA Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Multi-probe anechoic chamber (MPAC) is a widely used over the air (OTA) solution due to its advantage of controllability of channel environment reconstruction. In MPAC, it is meaningful to use a small number of probes in order to save the cost of hardware resources. This paper presents a new probe selection algorithm called the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) to obtain the angular positions and weights of the OTA probes. Simulation results show that the proposed probe configuration algorithm offers good channel emulation accuracy in terms of spatial correlation in the test area.

articleTitle: Path Loss Modeling Based on USRP-X410 and General Graph Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Path loss is a critical parameter in representing the characteristics of wireless channels and plays a pivotal role in wireless channel modeling. This paper introduces a novel method for path loss modeling, leveraging the general graph optimization (G2O) algorithm. Importantly, the data used for modeling were derived from extensive measurements using the USRP-X410 platform, which adds a unique element of practical applicability to our research. Two different models for indoor and outdoor scenarios were developed and optimized with this approach. The results indicate a significant reduction in modeling errors by using the G2O algorithm, effectively enhancing the accuracy of the path loss model.

articleTitle: Analysis and Study of Radiation Emission Measurement of Integrated Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In order to understand the electromagnetic emission generated by integrated circuit (IC), according to the coupling mode of IC generating electromagnetic emission, the measurement principle of electromagnetic emission of IC is analyzed, and the electromagnetic emission is measured on two IC. The measurement data shows that IC will produce significant electromagnetic emission. Through these measured analysis and research, IC manufacturers will value the electromagnetic compatibility of IC in the design process.

articleTitle: Broadband Generation of Dual Spin-Decoupled Beams by a Reception-to-Radiation Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband reception-to-radiation metasurface is introduced to generate dual spin-decoupled beams with high efficiency. With U-slot structure employed as the radiation patch, a reception-to-radiation metasurface element is designed with high transmission efficiency within a wide frequency band. Guided by a proposed spin-decoupled strategy, the designed element is configured to form a metasurface lens. With a horn feed located at the focal point of the lens, the assembled antenna can radiate dual beams respectively in the two spins with opposite chirality. Simulation results of the lens antenna show that a pencil beam in right hand circular polarization is deflected to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+x$</tex> direction with 20° away from the boresight of the aperture whereas a left hand circular polarization beam is tilted to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+y$</tex> direction with a deflection angle of 30°.

articleTitle: Quiet Zone Diagnostics in a Microwave Anechoic Chamber Using Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A quiet zone (QZ) diagnostic technique for a microwave anechoic chamber has been demonstrated. It provides a comprehensive imaging view of the QZ's performance. The imaging for reflected signals from different angles and direct signals within the QZ provides the location of strong reflected signals accurately. This technology can perform a specific diagnosis of the QZ after it is found that the performance of the quiet zone does not meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: Self-Defense Interference Cancellation Algorithm Based on Virtual Segmented Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The suppression of self-defense main lobe interference (SD-MLI) through space time coding (STC) waveform has been proven to be an effective method. However, when the signal of interest (SOI) is not a single-tone signal but with a certain baseband bandwidth, it cannot strictly meet the narrowband characteristics that is, use phase shift to represent the delay of the signal. To overcome this issue, this paper proposes a self-defense interference cancellation method based on virtual segmentation. By segmenting the received signal according to the “time-frequency” relationship, the SOI within each segmented signal regains good narrowband characteristics, thereby preserving SOI more completely while cancelling interference signals. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the algorithm, as the number of codes increases, the cancellation effect gradually recovers, but the proposed method belongs to quantitative variation which has certain engineering limitations.

articleTitle: Wide-Stopband EMI Filter Based on Coaxial Metal-Dielectric EBG Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A wide-stopband EMI filter based on a coaxial metal-dielectric electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure is presented in this paper. The effects of dielectric permittivity, dielectric thickness, inner diameter of the outer conductor, and periods on the stopband characteristics in limited length are investigated. Research has shown that increasing the dielectric constant of a medium or reducing the thickness of a dielectric can effectively broaden the stopband and enhance stopband attenuation in the frequency range of 1–20 GHz. Additionally, increasing the inner diameter of the outer conductor can further improve the filtering performance. Although loading more periods within limited space can achieve stopband attenuation exceeding 150 dB, it results in a higher lower cutoff frequency. For instance, when the number of periods is 20, the lower cutoff frequency is 5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Predicting High-Order Passive Intermodulation Products in Coaxial Connectors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Based on the polynomial model, a novel method for predicting the power of high-order passive intermodulation products is proposed. For the nonlinear characteristics of coaxial connectors, the test steps are shortened and the test data are divided into segmented intervals to perform curve fitting. A series of two-tone PIM tests, with input power ranging from 33 to 43 dBm in 0.25 dB steps, are conducted by selecting flanged SMA connectors as test samples. The prediction results of the proposed model are in good agreement with the test results, verifying the validity of the model. The differences between the proposed model and other nonlinear models are compared, and the root mean square error (RMSD) is introduced as the index to quantify the degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: A kind of Transparent Energy Selective Surface Design Method Based on Semiconductor Micro-Nano Hybrid Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the concept of a transparent energy selective surface (ESS) is proposed, which aims to provide a new electromagnetic protection technology for the photoelectric composite detection window. Through the micro nano hybrid integration process, the energy selective electromagnetic structure and diode devices are integrated and designed, utilizing the high transmittance characteristics of sapphire to achieve transparent design of ESS. The simulation results show that the designed transparent ESS can provide electromagnetic protection while also having good light transmittance.

articleTitle: Research on Differential Signal Wideband Common-Mode Suppression Filtering Cable
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In order to improve the reliability of electronic circuits, differential transmission technology is gradually applied to the transmission of high-speed digital signals. Compared with a single transmission line, the transmission of differential pairs has great advantages in anti-noise, anti-crosstalk, EMI. However, in the actual circuit, there will inevitably be some unbalanced factors, causing part of the differential signal to become common mode noise, which will affect the transmission of useful signals and destroy the signal integrity of the differential signal. How to effectively reduce the EMI of the differential signal and improve the anti-interference ability of the differential signal under the premise of ensuring the integrity of the differential signal is an urgent problem in the field of differential signal processing.compact planar dual-band filters.

articleTitle: Stable Remote Receiving System with Different Down-conversion Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: We present a time-stable remote receiving system for X-band radar signals. The transmission delay variation of the broadband signal is compensated for at the local end with a synchronized sample clock. The X-band signal is down-converted with three distinct methods at the electrical or optical domain. Experimentally, a root mean square (RMS) timing jitter of less than 10 ps is achieved for the radar signal after 25 km fiber transmission. This comparison provides insights and guidance for the design of remote ends for a multi-antenna distributed receiving system.

articleTitle: An equivalent method for shielding performance of vertical layered carbon fiber composites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: For vertically laminated carbon fiber reinforced polymer (VL CFRP), the traditional homogenization method is to equip them with multilayer anisotropic uniform media. In this paper, a new equivalent model is proposed, the complex dielectric constant of the radius direction of carbon fiber and the direction of the axis of carbon fiber is calculated by using the average field theory to characterize the complex structure inside CFRP, and a uniform medium of single-layer uniaxial anisotropy is obtained. The shielding efficiency (SE) of the VL CFRP model, the proposed equivalent model and the traditional equivalent model is solved by FEKO respectively, it was found that in the frequency range of 15 to 40 GHz, the proposed equivalent model was more accurate and simpler in structure than the traditional equivalent model.

articleTitle: The Research on a Method for Measuring Harmonic Emission of Millimeter Radar by Compact Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Compact Range is widely used for antenna measurements. However, it is rarely used in EMC test. We propose a compact range method for measuring harmonic emission of millimeter radar. According to the characteristic of the compact range, we re-derive the calculation formula, research the test procedure and analyze the dynamic range. Typical radars are selected for testing.

articleTitle: Broadband Microwave Photonic Phase Shifter with a Full 360° Phase Tunable Range Based on Dual-Parallel Mach-Zehnder Modulator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A photonic phase shifter suitable from single frequency signals to broadband signals is proposed. In this system, the broadband signal phase obtained by optical heterodyne using LO signals has 360° adjustability.

articleTitle: NLOS Wireless Localization Algorithm Based on Ray-tracing and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Most of the existing localization algorithms are for line-of-sight (LOS) condition. However, the localization errors of the existing algorithms are not reliable for non-line-of-sight (NLOS) condition. This paper performs wireless channel measurements in campus scenario at 3.3 GHz. The campus scenario contains both LOS and NLOS conditions. Measured channel impulse responses (CIRs) are utilized for electromagnetic (EM) parameter calibration based on ray-tracing (RT) simulation. After that, RT simulation provides accurate path loss information of each point in the campus scenario. Path loss fingerprint dataset is built for neural network training. The paper proposes a residual neural network with 12 layers for NLOS wireless localization. The residual neural network achieves a 4 meters localization minimum error, 6 meters localization mean error, and 5 meters localization root-mean-square error in the campus scenario. Consequently, the proposed wireless localization algorithm is practical and effective for the scenario with NLOS condition.

articleTitle: An Analog-Digital Mixed Self-Interference Cancellation Method for Full-Duplex Short-Wave Radios
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Full duplex radio is one of the key technologies for future wireless communications. The radiation from the co-located high-power transmitter induces serious self-interference to the high sensitivity receiver. In order to cancel the self-interference., a digital-controlled analog interference cancellation system is proposed. The time delay alignment of the proposed self-interference cancellation system is analyzed. By using the digital time delay method., the time delay differential of the analog circuits is successfully compensated. By using the proposed interference cancellation system with time delay alignment., a good interference cancellation performance is observed.

articleTitle: Research on Equivalent Modeling and Simulation Method of Surface Current Distribution of Metal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Due to the imbalance of ground potential between the grounding points of various electrical equipment, current is often formed on the surface of ship, causing electromagnetic compatibility problems. It is necessary to carry out modeling and simulation research on surface current distribution. In this paper, an equivalent modeling and simulation method for the surface current distribution of metal materials based on partial element equivalent circuit method is proposed, and the metal material is converted into an equivalent circuit model and the surface current distribution is simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network-Based Digital Twin Modeling Method for All-Optical Matching System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In practical applications, the dispersion of high order nonlinear fiber (HNLF) and erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) will introduce new noise, which may lead to misjudgment of matching results. In this research, based on the actual demand, the multi-layer deep neural network with parallel input is used to model the all-optical matching system based on different matching formats such as OOK, BPSK, QPSK. Experimental results show that this method has a very low bit error rate, can achieve accurate transmission, and greatly simplify our experimental steps. This technique serves as a potential choice for future simulation methods and system modeling.

articleTitle: Simulation and experiment of microstrip lines temperature rise based on COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Conductor loss and dielectric loss of the microstrip line can lead to temperature rise and limit the power capacity of the microstrip circuit. This involves the interaction (coupling) between the electric and temperature fields. In this study, the factors affecting the temperature rise of the microstrip line were analyzed by means of the parallel plate model. In addition, based on COMSOL Multiphysics simulation software, the influence of dielectric dissipation factor tanδ of microstrip lines of FR4 and RO4350B on the temperature rise per unit input power (TRPIP) was simulated. The simulation results under the set basic parameters show that the TRPIP of the strip conductors of the FR4-substrate microstrip lines with tanδ of 0.02 is about 4.8 °C, and that of RO450B-substrate microstrip lines with tanδ of 0.0037 is about 1.38 °C. Finally, in order to verify the simulation results, a non-invasive measuring device with an infrared camera was constructed to measure the heat distribution on the surface of the microstrip line.

articleTitle: Improved response of TVS and PIN diode combined electromagnetic protection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: To combat the interference and damage caused by external EMP, TVS and PIN diodes, two common electromagnetic protection components, are frequently used together. However, in practical applications, it is found that the PIN diode in the combined protection circuit is turned on first and TVS does not play a role. This study examines this phenomenon using the TVS-TVS3V3L4U and PIN diode-SMP1320. The findings indicate that adding capacitance and resistance between the TVS and PIN diode can successfully solve the problem. The findings of this study have some reference value for powerful EMP protection.

articleTitle: Doppler Frequency Shift Simulator based on swept-wavelength laser
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a photonic-assisted Doppler frequency shift simulator is proposed. The input microwave signal is modulated to the swept-wavelength optical carrier and transmitted through the dispersion medium. After optoelectronic conversion, the frequency-translated signal is generated. Results on the proposed frequency shift simulator demonstrate frequency translation of dual-band radar signal of S-band and X-band. The equivalent velocity of the dual band signal varied from 11m/s to 1263m/s in the experiment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Diagnosis of RF Circuits Based on Near Field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is widely spread in the circuit system, arose from the parasitic inductance and parasitic capacitance in the circuit. The voltage and current of the integrated circuit (IC) would change dramatically when processing high-frequency signals, electromagnetic radiation or EMI is prominent for the IC when working on the operating frequency of megahertz. In this paper, based on the surface Hugen's equivalence principle, the method of the radiation equivalent source being equivalent to the electric source and the magnetic source is proposed. The method is verified based on data extracted from the CST Studio Suite which is sampled from the radiation pattern of different RF circuit and components. By collecting the Near Field Scanning information to build an accurate equivalent source, the method can precisely reconstruct the electromagnetic field around the circuits.

articleTitle: Gain Boosting Technique for Flapping Wing Surface Integrated Antenna based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: To facilitate the heightened integration of the Micro Aerial Vehicle (MAV) system and bolster the stability of remote communication with the ground, a technique that aims to boost the gain of flapping wing surface integrated antenna by loading metasurface is proposed. The reflective metasurface and the antenna are placed on the upper and lower surface of the wings respectively. Based on the in-phase reflective properties of the metasurface, the effect of reducing the backward radiation and enhancing the forward radiation of the antenna are realized, so that the antenna radiation beam is directly adjusted to improve the gain performance. The results show that the antenna loaded with metasurface operates stably in 5G-n78/n79 and ISM-5.8GHz bands, and has excellent gain improvement effect within the range of wing flapping angles. At the resonant frequency, there is a maximum increase of 5.28dB in gain. The directivity of the antenna varies with the change of angles between the metasurface and the antenna, providing an effective beam scanning capability.

articleTitle: An Evaluation Method of Vehicle Radiation Emission Measurement System in SAC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Vehicle radiation emission is usually tested in a semi-anechoic chamber (SAC). The measurement system including the test site, the measurement receiver, the antennas, the connection cables, and other items within the test site, will all affect the measurement results. In the daily work, it is not convenient for the laboratory to confirm the normalised site attenuation (NSA) of the SAC by comparing it with that of the open-area test site (OATS) before each test. In order to guarantee the accuracy and consistency of the measurement results, a method using a comb signal generator as a reference radiation source is presented in this paper. And the maximum limit and minimum limit of the reference generator's radiation emission are obtained through the statistical analysis. The average values and standard deviations are calculated from many sets of independent measurement data. And the half width of the interval corresponding to 95% probability is less than 3dB, thus the maximum limit and minimum limit are defined. Furthermore, a measurement example is performed to show how to find the anormal points which is greater than the maximum limit or less than the minimum limit and ensure the accuracy of the measurement results by adjusting the measurement system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Mainlobe Cancellation Technique Under Non-Ideal Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Mainlobe cancellation technique can suppress mainlobe jamming while maintaining undistorted monopulse ratio for unbiased angle estimation. In this paper, quantitative analysis of mainlobe cancellation technique in the presence of amplitude-phase error is studied. By establishing the model of mainlobe cancellation for monopulse at subarray level, the concept of angular resolution of mainlobe cancellation is proposed and the impact of amplitude-phase error on the accuracy of angle estimation is analyzed. Numerical simulations have verified the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: K-band microwave generation using a MgF2 soliton microcomb
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The microwave signal source is one of the core components of electronic information systems. With the improvement of communication data capacity and radar detection accuracy, modern communication and radar systems have put forward higher requirements for the frequency and phase noise level of local oscillator microwave signals. Recent developments in optical frequency combs have provided a high-performance approach with compact size for microwave signal generation. Here, we prepared a K-band microwave signal generator based on the MgF2 soliton microcomb. The generated 24 GHz microwave signal has a phase noise level of −119 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset frequency, comparable to current electronic microwave sources. Through the optimization of the microresonator structure, the phase noise can be potentially reduced to the quantum noise limit.

articleTitle: Measurement and Simulation of AeroMACS Signal Coverage for Airplane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: AeroMACS (Aeronautical Mobile Airport Communication System) is the next-generation airport communication system, and it is necessary to study its signal coverage characteristics for increasing the communication quality. In this paper, the Boeing B737-400 airplane's fuselage, cabin, and luggage compartment are modeled by its constituting objects, such as position, sitting chair, windows, ground and etc. The AeroMACS signal coverage around and inside the airplane is simulated with the illuminating angles. The effectiveness of the model is proven by the actual measuring results of the most simplified AeroMACS network. Subsequently, more signal coverage scenarios are simulated using the model, and some characteristics of AeroMACS signal coverage for airplane are obtained. From the analysis of simulation results, in most cases, the signal strength difference between different positions of the luggage compartment or cabin of the airplane is small. However, the relative position relationship between the base station and the airplane has a more significant impact on the signal coverage results.

articleTitle: Photonic-assisted self-interference cancellation frequency downconverter for radio-over-fiber transmissions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A photonic-assisted self-interference cancellation downconverter for radio-over-fiber transmissions is proposed. In this work, a dual-parallel dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator (DP-DMZM) is used to achieve carrier-suppressed single sideband modulation (CS-SSB), which achieves self-interference cancellation (SIC) in the optical domain. Meanwhile, the proposed system can downconvert the transmitted signal and overcome the chromatic dispersion-induced power fading (CDIP). The simulation results show that the proposed SIC scheme has a large operating bandwidth and high transmission quality. The cancellation depth of wideband SIC can be greater than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Manipulation of Analog Sensors through Electromagnetic Interference Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Analog sensors connect the physical world and the cyber world. They convert physical quantities into corresponding analog electrical quantities, which are then further digitized and read by a controller. Electromagnetic interference (EMI) attacks will trigger the electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) of analog sensors, resulting in false output values. In two experimental cases, we arbitrarily modify the sensor output by adjusting the frequency and level of the EMI signal. Results show that the analog sensor output can be effectively manipulated through EMI attacks.

articleTitle: Long-Term Stable Optoelectronic Oscillator Based on Phase-Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: We demonstrate an optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) based on a phase-locked loop and an optical delay line to enhance its long-term stability. By detecting the phase of a single-frequency probe signal and compensating for the delay variation of the resonant cavity, a 10 GHz OEO is obtained with improved phase noise at the low offset frequency. The Allan deviation of OEO reaches 1.36E-15 at the average time of 400 s. The long-term stability of the OEO meets the strict requirements of applications in radar, signal processing, and precise measurements.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis for the Resolution of the Spatial-Polarization Combined Anti-Interference Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The spatial-polarization combined anti-interference (SPCAI) technology can distinguish and cancel interference signals by using spatial information and polarization information. In order to improve the ability of the SPCAI technology to distinguish target signals from interference signals, this paper first established the spatial-polarization resolution model. The mathematical expressions of the resolution in SPCAI technology are derived, and the quantitative description method of the resolution is proposed. Then, based on the mathematical expressions, the factors that affect the resolution of SPCAI technology are analyzed. It is found that with the increase of the elements spacing, the resolution of SPCAI technology shows a tendency of oscillation increase. Finally, the resolution of the four-element alternate polarization array is simulated numerically. The simulation results are consisted with the theoretical analysis, which proves the validity of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Modal Decomposition Method for Fast and Efficient PCB Modeling and Signal Integrity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: An AI-enhanced modal decomposition method is proposed in this paper for fast and efficient high-speed multilayered PCB modeling and integrity. Depending on modal patterns of PCB local structures, modal decomposition method divides a given high-speed PCB interconnections into independent modal cells, and take advantages of different evaluation methods (analytical, numerical, AI-based) to analyze each modal cell. With the assistance of AI technology, compound methods find a way to compute complex PCB structures effectively in this modal decomposition method. We briefly introduced the architecture and workflow of the proposed method, and then gave a practical application example to show the validity. Data show frequency error of 2.3/1.4% and amplitude error of 0.3/0.6dB for 0-28/28-40GHz between measurement and model prediction, showing great potentials of the AI-enhanced modal decomposition method for PCB modeling and signal integrity.

articleTitle: A Small Open TEM Chamber Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: TEM chamber is a commonly used electromagnetic field generating device, this paper establishes a three-dimensional model of a TEM chamber with conical transition segments at both ends and open sides of the outer conductor, and designs the TEM chamber by calculating the characteristic impedance of the TEM chamber by changing the aspect ratio of the width of the core plate to the height from the pole plate<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1], [2]</sup>. In this paper, the S-parameters and field distribution of the TEM chamber are investigated and analysed. CST electromagnetic simulation software is used to simulate the cross-sectional field distribution of the chamber and the effect of the addition of EUT on the field distribution of the TEM chamber. The width of the core plate inside the TEM chamber has a large effect on the characteristic impedance, which decreases with the increase of the core plate width. The core plate width of 325 mm is used to calculate the characteristic impedance of the TEM chamber. When the core plate width is 325 mm, the characteristic impedance of the main transmission section of the TEM chamber is 75 Ω, the S11 is less than −15 dB, and the voltage VSWR is less than 1.5.

articleTitle: Design of Filtering Power Amplifier Based on a Novel Band-pass Impedance Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This article presents a novel band-pass filtering impedance transformer (BFIT) with the transformer ratio from 0.1 to 10. This BFIT is composed of two stepped impedance resonators (SIRs) which are cascaded and electric coupled. The analytical formulas and design steps of BFIT are given, and the impedance transformer (IT) is used in the design of a band-pass filtering power amplifier (PA). Finally, a 2.31-2.36 GHz band-pass filtering PA with measured drain efficiency of 54%-64% and large-signal gain of 11.2-11.5 dB is designed, fabricated and measured. Besides, the designed PA shows a good band-pass filtering characteristic, and achieves out-of-band suppression of 25 dB and 53 dB in the upper and lower sidebands.

articleTitle: Field Trials of Communication and QoT Estimation over an SDM Optical Fiber Cable Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: We have successfully demonstrated field high-capacity communication experiments and the autonomous lightpath configuration by Quality-of-Transmission (QoT) estimation within the Space Division Multiplexing (SDM) network utilizing deployed seven-core fibers.

articleTitle: Parity-Time-Symmetric Optoelectronic Oscillator Based on DPMZM With Single-Sideband Suppressed-Carrier Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A Parity-time (PT) symmetric optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) based on dual-parallel Mach-Zehnder modulator (DPMZM) with single-sideband suppressed-carrier modulation is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. PT symmetry is realized in a single physical loop, where the gain and loss loops are formed by the beating between the optical carrier and the ±1st-order sideband. By adjusting the bias point voltage of the DPMZM, the gain and loss can be balanced to achieve single-mode oscillation. In our experiment, the system produces a microwave signal with a frequency of 10.79 GHz, which phase noise is about −111dBc/Hz when the offset frequency is 10kHz.

articleTitle: Study on the Ball Grid Array Connection Failure Effects on Near Magnetic Field Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: As one of the most important packaging methods, ball grid array (BGA) is widely used in various integrated circuits. In this paper, the BGA connection failure effects on near magnetic field radiation are studied. A BGA transition structure within printed circuit boards (PCB) was modeled and analyzed based on electromagnetic simulation. The simulation results are verified by the very near scanning measurement. The results prove that the failure of BGA ground solder balls will cause the increase of near magnetic field radiation. And the near magnetic field intensity increases with the increase of the number of ground solder ball failures. In addition, the failure of the ground solder ball leading to the coupling of external field strength into the PCB board is experimental analyzed.

articleTitle: An Omnidirectional Multi-Band Electrically Small Antenna Fed by Coplanar Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an omnidirectional multiband electrically small antenna fed by coplanar waveguide has been proposed. We load corrugated metal ring structure with supporting spoof localized surface plasmons based on the traditional monopole antenna fed by coplanar waveguide. That not only maintains the characteristics of the omni-directivity of the antenna, but also reduces the electrical size of the antenna and generates multiple frequency bands. The impedance matching is further improved and the gain at high frequency is increased by loading a half of elliptic-shaped slot at the terminal of the corrugated metal ring structure. The performance of the antenna is verified by CST software. The resonant frequency points are 0.87GHz, 1.73GHz and 2.42GHz, respectively. The corresponding gains are 0.676dBi, 1.1dBi and 2.94dBi, respectively. The proposed antenna has a broad application in the field of base station antenna, electromagnetic compatibility and Internet of Things.

articleTitle: Robust Wireless Power Transfer Based on a Needle Beam Generated by a Transmissive Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: To achieve a long-distance robust wireless power transfer (WPT) in the microwave band, a transmissive metasurface that can tightly focus vector beams is presented in this paper. We first design a unit cell that can independently and simultaneously control the phase and polarization of the transmitted wave. Then, a metasurface is constructed by the designed unit cell according to the required polarization and phase distribution. Finally, a focused needle beam with a small full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) is obtained. The needle beam is non diffractive in a distance about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.8\ \lambda$</tex>, which is suitable for robust WPT. The proposed design method paves a new way for the WPT systems based on vector beams.

articleTitle: Uncertainty assessment of SAR measurement system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: With the widespread use of wireless devices, the potential harm of electromagnetic radiation from electronic devices to human health has attracted increasing attention. International standards require the evaluation of electromagnetic radiation safety of wireless devices through Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) measurements. Due to the inherent contradiction between signal coverage and radiation intensity, SAR values closely related to wireless device radiation intensity often approach the regulatory limits. To avoid misjudgment, it is essential to ensure the accuracy of the measurement system. This paper provides a comprehensive and in-depth analysis of the uncertainty associated with SAR measurements. The uncertainty of measurement results is influenced by both the stability of the tested device and the performance of the measurement system itself. Based on a thorough analysis of the measurement system validation experiments, this paper delves into the assessment of uncertainties introduced by the measurement system. As these uncertainties are independent of the device being tested, their evaluation holds more general significance, thereby establishing a solid foundation for the analysis and optimization of measurement systems.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Wide-Slot Planar Antenna for Dual-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A CPW-fed wide-slot dual-band antenna is presented. The proposed dual-band antenna consists of a lower band element and two identical upper band elements by sharing the structure. The upper band antenna is placed on the ground of the lower band antenna to achieve miniaturization. The simulated results show that the bandwidth of the dual-band antenna in the lower band and the upper band are 117.8% (0.698-2.7 GHz) and 58.1% (3.3-6 GHz), and the isolation between three ports is greater than 15 dB. The proposed antenna achieves simple structure, broadband dual-band and better radiation efficiency in a specific direction with an overall size of 0.26λ × 0.24λ ×0.002λ (λ is the free-space wavelength at the lowest frequency).

articleTitle: Radio Environment Map Construction by Residual Kriging Based on Bayesian Hierarchical Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, the Bayesian hierarchical model (BHM) for the propagation parameters based on the prior information and measurements is conducted, and posterior inferences are also processed by the Gibbs sampling. After the inference of pathloss component, shadow fading component is estimated via the Kriging interpolation in accordance with measurement residuals. What's more, the radio environment map (REM) is obtained by these two components. Finally, the superiority of proposed algorithm in accuracy to others can be evaluated by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A method for Orthopedic Robot Remote Operation Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Orthopedics robots have become a new direction for orthopedic surgery in recent years and have achieved accuracy and personalization of surgery to the greatest extent, which has opened a new path for the development of orthopedic surgery. The rapid deployment of 5G network infrastructure will effectively promote high-end medical resources to sink to the grass roots. The performance of orthopedic robots has a direct impact on surgical effects, precise testing and objective evaluation are an important foundation for improving robot's performance. This thesis analyzes its technical status in terms of application scenarios, networking architecture, performance indicators, and test methods, aiming to build a testing environment, test and analyze orthopedic robots in different application scenarios and network configurations, and explore the performance effects and future optimization direction.

articleTitle: Link Budget Calculation for LoRa-band Remoting Sensing Satellite
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Small satellites are increasingly attracting the attention of the industry for its many aspects of advantages. We proposed a communication subsystem for commercial remote sensing satellite. The interface between the communication system and other modules on the satellite and the communication protocol are briefly introduced. In order to make sure that the satellite-to-ground link is reliable, we calculate the link budget at 471 MHz for LEO small satellite. Additionally, the transmission power and reception sensitivity is 17 dBm and −123 dBm respectively. The result shows that the proposed subsystem is reliable in RF performance and can be used in other commercial satellite in the future.

articleTitle: Sharing and compatibility Study of Fixed Satellite service Earth Station and Mobile service operating in the frequency band 3 600–3 800 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The frequency band 3 600–3 800 MHz, as part of C band, is the candidate frequency band to IMT identification for global harmonization. From the Radio Regulation, Fixed Satellite service has been allocated as primary service for all the three regions, while the MS service is secondary service in Region1. To ensure protection of those services to which the frequency band is allocated on a primary basis and not impose undue constraints on the existing services and their future development, the sharing and compatibility studies should be conducted. This paper provides one of study case between the Fixed Satellite service Earth Station and Mobile service operating in the frequency band 3 600–3 800 MHz.

articleTitle: Research on Anti-strong Electromagnetic pulse Technology for Power Port of Land Warfare Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Strong Electromagnetic pulse can easily be coupled to the internal circuit of the land combat platform through antenna, aperture, cable, etc., interfering with the normal operation of electronic equipment, and even causing permanent damage. This article designs a multi-level filtering protection circuit for the power port of the vehicle platform in response to the protection requirements of the power port of the land combat platform. The generation mechanism and modulation mode of strong Electromagnetic pulse are analyzed, and the electromagnetic coupling mode of the power port of the land combat platform is studied. The strong Electromagnetic pulse protection circuit of the power port of the land combat platform is emphatically designed. The simulation test shows that the filtering effect of the strong Electromagnetic pulse protection circuit of the power port of the land combat platform can be as high as 60dB, which can protect the electronic equipment in the land combat platform very well, thus greatly improving the survivability of the land combat platform in the complex electromagnetic environment of the battlefield.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Absorber for Radiation Suppression in the Chip Package
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this page, a miniaturized absorber with ultrawide absorption band is designed and applied for radiation leakage suppression in the chip package. The proposed unit is a double-layer structure with two patterned resistive films of ITO etched on top of the dielectric substrate. The patterned layer is composed of a meandering square ring and a centric circular patch which enhances the coupling within the unit and facilitates the miniaturization of the structure. The size of the unit is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.08\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}\times 0.08\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}(\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}$</tex> is the wavelength in the free space of the lowest absorption frequency).
