When the periodic boundary condition is set in the simulation, it shows a broad absorption band <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{S}_{11}\leq-10\text{dB})$</tex> covering 23.8-40 GHz. This unit is then used as a square ring structure for radiation suppression in chip package which demonstrates a −10dB bandwidth within 25.5-39.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Rectification Case of Electromagnetic Compatibility Conducted Emission of a Vehicle Projection Lamp
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The automotive electronics (projection lamp) was tested according to the requirements of GB 18655–2002 “Limits and methods of measurement of radio disturbance characteristics for the protection of receivers used on board wehicles”, and the test result of conducted emission voltage method was higher than the test limit, which did not meet the requirements of the standard. The main circuit of the projection lamp contains a buck DC/DC converter, which drives the LED with constant current. Conduct conducted emission fault diagnosis by analyzing the conducted emission checklist and the cause of non-conformity, and finally find the interference source through the analysis of test data and the targeted analysis of characteristic spectrum, and make the conducted emission voltage method of the projection lamp meet the limit requirements of Class 5 of GB 18655–2002 standard with the minimum engineering cost.

articleTitle: Time-Frequency Analysis of the Optical Signal from Lightning Return Stroke Channel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The time-frequency analysis (TFA) method is employed to analyze the optical radiation of return strokes in a rocket-triggered lightning. The results show that the arrival time of different frequency components of the optical radiation presents nonmonotonic variation with the increase of the frequency, which might have an intrinsic relationship with the equivalent distribution circuit of the channel.

articleTitle: An Antenna Design Method Based on Stacking Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Antenna design is an important part of the communication system. In this paper, an antenna design method based on stacking model is proposed, which can provide suitable size parameters according to the given performance indicators. We have validated using a horn antenna, using 80% of the data as the training set and 20% of the data as the test set. Given the antenna gain, bandwidth, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>and resonance point to predict the length and aperture diameter of the horn antenna, the resulting average absolute age percentage error (MAPE) is 0.0136, and the operating time is about 2 seconds. This method has good prediction accuracy and fast running speed. At the same time, by comparing with other models, the superiority of the method is verified, which is reflected in the great improvement of prediction accuracy and efficiency, and the method has good applicability to other antennas.

articleTitle: Gain Enhanced Differential-Fed Circular Patch Antenna With Generated Radiation Nulls
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a gain enhanced differential-fed circular patch antenna with generated H-plane radiation nulls. By deploying the meticulously tuned parasitic metallic strips above the bottom patch, three effective equivalent magnetic currents could be easily pronounced. Together with the extra peripheral magnetic currents produced by the bottom patch, a holistic array factor analysis could be conducted in order to show the mechanism for the generation of H-plane nulls, which accounts for the enhancement of gain performance. Finally, a prototype is designed and fabricated. The measured results clearly show the two paired H-plane nulls and the peak gain value could be incremented to 9.3 dBi.

articleTitle: Conduct, Results and Analysis of Biennial Proficiency Tests of SAR Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Specific absorption rate (SAR) measurements are routinely performed on wireless devices to assess its exposure. Proficiency tests (PTs) through interlaboratory comparison of SAR were conducted in 2017 and 2019. In total, 210 measurement results were provided in terms of best estimate and uncertainty. Firstly, the performance of all the participating laboratories are evaluated. Then this paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the PT results from three perspectives as follows, the applicability of performance statistics D% and z-score, the consistency of the PT results in 2017 and 2019, and the satisfaction rates of the PT results for GSM and LTE. Furthermore, to analyze the impacts of measurement conditions on the SAR, cross-correlations are calculated. It is shown that the SAR measurement is sensitive to the tissue equivalent liquid but insensitive to the environment temperature.

articleTitle: Problem Locating Method for PDN Structures with Segmentation Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The structure of power distribution network(PDN) is normally constructed with complex planes. The simulation and routing iteration process, which is a repetitive process for engineers, consumes a lot of time in the design phase. In addition, with the increase of transmission speed in electronic devices, PDN and decoupling capacitor optimization are necessary for product design. This paper presents a PDN analysis method that can be used to locate the problem positions of the PDN structure as well as PDN optimization without re-simulating the modified structure. In addition, since the segmentation technique is applied, it can be used for sensitivity analysis as well. The method is divided into three parts: Segmentation, Connection, and Calculation. The results are compared to commercial tools and achieve a good correlation.

articleTitle: A Five-Port UWB MIMO Slot Antenna Design with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper designs a high isolation five-port UWB MIMO slot antenna on FR4 substrate. The antenna structure with stepped slots can expand bandwidth to cover the frequency range of 1.7 GHz to 6 GHz. The proposed antenna reduces mutual coupling between antenna components by introducing a decoupling structure composed of symmetrical horizontal and vertical open slots, and the isolation is better than 15.33 dB throughout the entire operating bandwidth range. Meanwhile, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) of the antenna is less than 0.058, which is much lower than the specified 0.5, indicating the good performance of the MIMO antenna system.

articleTitle: Design of an Electromagnetic Pulse Radiation Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of poor low-frequency radiation performance of TEM horn antenna, the simulation optimization design is carried out. The low frequency compensation method of end loading resistance and back loading resistance is analyzed by using time domain analysis method, and the structural parameters such as the size of the TEM horn antenna and the top angle of the plate are optimized; the peak field strength and pulse width of the radiation field are improved by using the end crimping structure. The simulation results are verified by the measurement of the new antenna. The results show that the loading resistance can effectively reduce the reflection, and the peak field strength and pulse width of the back loading resistance are higher than that of the end loading resistance; the radiation performance of the antenna can be improved by appropriately increasing the antenna length, the top angle of the plate and the angle between the plates.

articleTitle: High-Capacity Photonic THz OAM Communication System Based on Broadband Huygens' Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a high-capacity photonic THz OAM wireless communication system based on a broadband Huygens' transmissive metasurface. The metasurface is designed to multiplex two distinct OAM beams with l=+1 and l=-1 operating at 0.1 THz, which has the advantages of low profile, simplicity, and ease of fabrication. Both simulation and measurement results indicate that it generates OAM beams with high purity over a broad bandwidth of 20 GHz (90–110 GHz). Crosstalk lower than −27 dB between the OAM modes can be achieved. Using the metasurface for a free-space link at a 0.1 THz carrier frequency, we achieve a 112 Gbit/s 16 quadrature amplitude modulation (16-QAM) data transmission with bit-error rates below 3.8e-3. This work verifies the feasibility of metasurface for high-capacity THz OAM communications, meaning it may open new opportunities for future THz communications.

articleTitle: Research on the Calibration Method of Low-Frequency Loop Antennas for Military Standard Tests
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Low-frequency loop antennas are important sensors for magnetic field radiation and immunity measurement in military standard tests. A loop antenna coefficient calibration method based on TEM cell is presented in this paper. The method adopts Gaussian process regression to correct the spatial wave impedance inside the TEM cell in the low-frequency. The TEM cell is used as a standard field strength generating device to calibrate the loop antenna coefficients when the operating frequency of the TEM cell is 10Hz~200kHz. The experimental results show that this method has good accuracy in the whole range of test frequency bands. It is an efficient and traceable method for calibrating the loop antenna coefficients.

articleTitle: On the Null Frequency Scanning Antenna: History, Theory and Recent Progress
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A mini-survey for null frequency scanning antennas (NFSAs) is presented in this article. NFSAs based upon different operation principles are classified and reviewed at first. Then, this article concentrates on the recent advances of multi-mode resonant null frequency scanning antennas (NFSAs). Mode synthesis design approach to NFSAs is introduced. Finally, possible developing trends of multi-mode resonant NFSAs are prospected.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Single-Port Measurement Campaign for Test System Calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A radio frequency (RF) test system is typically calibrated by a two-port network analyzer in conventional setups. However, the conventional calibration scheme becomes problematic for 5G base station (BS) test system as example due to setup complexity, cost and potential mismatch problems. A cost-effective single-port measurement scheme is presented in this paper. Based on the existing test system, the presented measurement scheme directly utilizes a single-port unit to calibrate the BS test system by three steps, i.e. unit self-calibration, switching matrix measurement and post-processing. The presented single-port measurement scheme is experimentally demonstrated to achieve the equivalent functionality as the conventional network analyzer scheme, reduce the measurement cost, while addressing the measurement inaccuracy introduced by the potential mismatching issue.

articleTitle: An optimization of GaN Physics-based Compact Model Based on Manifold Mapping Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: GaN physics-based compact models cannot be modelled without accurate structural parameters. In this paper, the structural parameters are optimised using a manifold mapping algorithm, with the compact model as the coarse model, the TCAD model as the fine model, and the real device as the target. When the fine model response agrees with the target response, the structural parameters are then determined. Finally, a genetic algorithm is used to make the coarse model response close to the fine model response, at which point the compact model modelling is completed.

articleTitle: Direct Power Injection Model for Integrated Circuits Immunity Simulation on Power Pins
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces a complete simulation model of a direct power injection (DPI) setup, used to measure the immunity of integrated circuits to conducted continuous-wave interference. This model encompasses the whole measurement setup itself as well as the integrated circuit under test and its environment (printed circuit board, power supply). A simple example about the methodology and several DPI simulation results are shown. Simulation results obtained from the model are compared with measurement results, and these demonstrate the validity of this approach. The combined model is able to predict the immunity level more precisely and better support the immunity simulation of circuit under direct power injection (DPI) test.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Fiber-Optic Ultrasonic Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) relies on the strongly localized evanescent field at the interface of the sensing material and coupling medium, and has been widely used in photoacoustic (PA) detection. And Surface plasmon resonance phenomenon is easily excited by TFBG. However, most of the current fiber laser-ultrasonic actuators only allow the effective generation of ultrasonic waves on the end face of the optical fiber and have never considered the effective combination of optical fiber and SPR optical phenomenon to generate ultrasonic waves. In this study, a tilted fiber Bragg grating (TFBG) plasmonic active ultrasonic actuator that matched the specific wavelength of the laser, which can effectively generate ultrasound in the side area of the TFBG, has been proposed and demonstrated. This novel and simple-to-manufacture TFBG-SPR laser-ultrasonic actuator have potential applications in fiber-optic ultrasonic testing technology.

articleTitle: EMC Simulation Analysis of Fuel Cell Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In order to study the electromagnetic compatibility of fuel cell vehicle, DC/DC converter in fuel cell vehicle is used as the interference source. Based on obtained interference current signal and reference point radiation field strength of the wiring harness port during operation of DC/DC converter, electromagnetic radiation emission simulation model of DC/DC converter is established, and the model is verified by experimental data. The overall variation trend of the simulation results is consistent with the measured results, and the average error is about 5dB in the high-frequency band. Then, the model is put into the vehicle model as an interference source. The simulation result shows that with the increase of frequency, the surface current of vehicle body is also gradually increasing, and the existence of the metal body hinders the radiation emission of the internal interference source. In addition, the existence of body surface current will also cause secondary radiation. Finally, the electromagnetic field at the head position of the driver and passenger in vehicle is analyzed and compared with GB 8702–2014 standard. The simulation results show that the electric field strength and the magnetic field strength both meet the standard.

articleTitle: Impact of Place and Route Position on FPGA Electromagnetic Emission Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The continual advancement in the integration density of integrated circuit (IC) and their decreasing size augments device performance. However, this progression introduces pronounced challenges in terms of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). EMC issues have now become pivotal factors that influence not just individual circuit functionalities but even the overall system's operation. Given the significance of this, the study of electromagnetic characteristics of IC is of great significance. This paper investigates the electromagnetic emission (EME) Characteristics of FPGA from the perspective of place and route (P&R) positions. The obtained results indicate that alterations in the P&R positions can affect the overall EME level of the FPGA. Placement and routing on the lower side of the FPGA will result in a smaller EME level. While such positional changes don't substantially impact the EME spectral characteristics of the FPGA, they do affect its spatial distribution characteristics of the EME.

articleTitle: Design of Coupling/Decoupling Networks for Differential Mode Disturbance Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a set of 10 Ω-50 Ω impedance converting baluns and a coupling/decoupling network (CDN) for differential-mode conducted disturbance testing are designed. The transmission line transformer theory is used to improve the impedance-converting balun, which broadens the operating frequency of baluns and offers a tolerance for the CDN's calibration. With the use of baluns and a vector network analyzer, the two-port insertion loss of the CDN is calculated, and the experimental findings meet the needs of differential mode conducted disturbances and signaling immunity test equipment at AC power ports,

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge Parameter Prediction based on DALSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: To improve accuracy and convergence speed of predicting variation of electrostatic discharge parameters, with Double Attention mechanism, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network time series prediction model (DALSTM) was proposed in this paper. By introducing the LSTM cell structure reconstructed with the attention mechanism, the model parameters are reduced to improve the convergence speed, and the self-attention layer calculates the self-attention weights on the output of each hidden layer to make full use of the cellular memory information and improves the prediction accuracy. After analysis using data from experiment results with the new system testing electrode moving velocity effect, proposed DALSTM model, compared to LSTM model, has indicators to be reduced to 62.77% in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), 74.56% in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and 74.58% in Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), respectively. There is also a significant improvement compared to other benchmark methods.

articleTitle: Conducted Electromagnetic Interference Modelling of an Automotive Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: The prediction of electromagnetic interference (EMI) for products in the testing environment has always been a key concern for auto parts manufacturers. This paper proposes a fast and accurate simulation method for conducted EMI interference based on the CISPR25 standard for printed circuit board (PCB). To strictly comply with the testing process, a program is developed using the FFT algorithm to simulate the measurement receiver for conducted interference. The main sources of EMI noise in gear and warning light indicators are analyzed. To simplify the EMI model, the physical PCB model is replaced with an equivalent SPICE model, which greatly reduces the number of the mesh grids, but still reckons the trace impedance in the PCB. In case the parasitic parameters between the PCB and the testing table are left out, the high-frequency parasitic parameters are deduced theoretically and modeled for the gear and warning light system. The resonance frequencies of the multi-wire's impedance are derived and validated. Combining the LISN, high-frequency wire model, testing table, and circuit model, a conducted interference simulation model for the gear and warning light indicators is constructed. The simulation results show high correlation with the measured results.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Influence Factors and Research Status of Non-contact Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: In different fields such as aerospace, petrochemical, military defense, and scientific research, etc., the protection of various electronic instruments and electrical equipment against electrostatic hazards is a widespread concern. This paper attempts to make a preliminary analysis of the influencing factors of non-contact electrostatic discharge, including the interaction of various related physical quantities and research status. The relationship between electrode moving speed and electrostatic discharge parameters is very importantly discussed. At the same time, the brief introduction is given to the physical and mathematical models and experimental devices commonly used in electrostatic discharge research, hoping to lay the groundwork for future research.

articleTitle: Ray Tracing Acceleration Method Based on Multilayer Dynamic Space Divisions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 7th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (ISEMC)
abstract: A ray tracing acceleration method based on multi-layer dynamic space divisions is proposed in this paper. The proposed method involves vertically layering the 3D model of the industrial scene and dynamically employing space divisions of the quadtree to each layer in an adaptive manner. During the ray tracing process, only the surface and edge information of the geometric objects stored in the node corresponding to the small division region intersected by the ray need to be considered. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed ray tracing acceleration algorithm maintains the same computational accuracy as the traditional ray tracing algorithm, while improving the computational efficiency to a certain extent. As the complexity of the 3D model increases, the number of intersections of reflections can be significantly reduced, resulting in a remarkable reduction of 50%-60% in overall ray tracing time. This mentioned approach helps to effectively reduce the number of intersection operations and computational complexity of ray tracing in the 3D industrial factory environment.
